papers.title: A level is not a rank: an empirical audit of quantile-to-index conversion in 10 released conformal-prediction libraries
papers.abstract: Context. A conformal interval at 0.90 keeps that guarantee only at the right rank: a fresh score falls at or below the rth smallest of n with probability r/(n + 1). The libraries we study instead hand a level to a quantile function, which can land elsewhere. At n = 20, the upper end of statsforecast's interval sits at position 18.05 where rank 19 is required. Objective. Where does installed code resolve the wrong rank, at what cost in coverage, and what does it return when no rank reaches the level? Method. We audit 39 sites where a level becomes an index in 10 pinned packages, a named set rather than a systematic search. 12 are classified by running them, 11 through their shared numpy method, the rest from source. Coverage is paired against the required rank on the same scores. Results. All 7 tabular implementations reach the required rank. In darts, on one code path, coverage is unchanged (0.0000) where the ranks agree and 0.0280 to 0.0560 lower where they differ; a second archive repeats that split but not its range. Below the feasibility floor, $n < 1/\alpha - 1$, of 14 public call paths 5 silently return a finite number; the rest raise or warn. Conclusions. Quantile interfaces take only a level; statsforecast's default calibrates below its floor. 6 of 19 upstream filings have merged, one fixing a coverage shortfall. A conformance suite classifies helpers by the rank they reach, and a checklist guides review.

papers.title: A Survey on RLOps for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become increasingly important for improving the reasoning, instruction-following, and task-solving capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, scaling RL training exposes failures in distributed execution, feedback computation, and learning dynamics that can waste computational resources, slow training, and undermine model improvements. These challenges have motivated a growing body of techniques for LLM RLOps, which manages the efficiency and reliability of operations throughout the LLM reinforcement learning training lifecycle. Despite growing interest, these techniques remain scattered across research areas, with limited synthesis of their operational roles and interactions. To bridge this gap, we present a systematic survey of LLM RLOps methods. We organize existing approaches into five stages: Training Setup, Experience Collection, Reward Computation, Policy Optimization, and Model Evaluation. Within each stage, we examine operational concerns, management techniques, and evaluation evidence. Building on this taxonomy, we identify open challenges and future directions in training process observability, cross-stage coordination, generalizable RLOps, multi-run management, and RLOps for recursive self-improvement. These directions extend operational management from individual training runs to diverse training settings, shared infrastructure, and successive improvement cycles. We maintain a GitHub repository indexing relevant papers and open resources at https://github.com/zhanglingzhe0820/Awesome-RLOps.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Model Predictive Control via Proximal Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Sampling-based model predictive control (MPC) enables real-time control of complex nonlinear systems but often incurs substantial computational costs due to repeated trajectory simulations. In this paper, we bridge policy optimization in reinforcement learning and sampling-based MPC to improve computational efficiency through sample reuse. Starting from a KL-regularized distributional formulation of trajectory optimization, we derive an exact performance-difference identity based on a signed exponential advantage function. This identity motivates two algorithms, PPO-MPPI and SPO-MPPI, which adapt proximal policy optimization techniques to sampling-based MPC, enabling multiple optimization updates using previously evaluated trajectories without additional forward simulations. We establish population-level monotonic improvement guarantees for both methods and prove convergence to first-order stationarity for PPO-MPPI under fixed-covariance Gaussian sampling distributions. Experiments on quadruped velocity tracking and quadrotor path tracking demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve competitive control performance at substantially lower computational cost than multi-stage sampling approaches. Our results establish a principled connection between policy optimization and sampling-based MPC and highlight the potential of trajectory reuse for sample-efficient predictive control.

authors.name: Jiarui Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Option-GRPO: Hierarchical RL Against AI Slop in Code Generation for Unseen SDKs
papers.abstract: Large language models increasingly produce AI slop in generated code: verbose, redundant, non-idiomatic implementations that pass functional checks but bloat codebases. The problem compounds on SDKs released after the model's training cutoff, where the model has neither idiomatic priors nor compositional understanding. We present Option-GRPO, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that adapts a code LLM to an unseen SDK from its source code alone, without human-written usage examples or test cases, and that explicitly optimizes for both functional correctness and code elegance. Our key insight is that SDK source code contains compositional structure that defines a hierarchy of reusable code patterns (code options) which simultaneously serve as the building blocks of a curriculum and the action space for efficient policy optimization. We show that code options induce a valid semi-Markov decision process, give conditional bounds under which shorter option description length implies more concise and, in expectation, more API-efficient programs, and analyze under stated assumptions how the option hierarchy improves credit assignment by a factor of $\sqrt{T/K}$. Using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with execution-based rewards at each curriculum level, Option-GRPO discovers SDK idioms, composes them into patterns, and assembles patterns into complete programs. Experiments on 12 unseen SDKs with a 32B-parameter base model demonstrate 61.4% pass@1, outperforming flat GRPO by 8.7 points, ExploraCoder by 11.2 points, and ReCode by 6.3 points. Option-GRPO produces solutions that use 34.7% fewer API calls and are 27% shorter than flat-GRPO outputs while maintaining higher correctness, directly attacking the slop problem.

papers.title: PRISM: Profiling and Representation of Individual Stereotypical Motion
papers.abstract: An anatomical pose provides interpretable joint structure, but no fixed set of physical landmarks can fully specify a person's movement. We introduce PRISM, a complementary representation that characterizes repetitive movement using tracked masks and dense optical flow. Torso-relative flow measures intensity, frame-wise mask variation measures spatial extent, signed-flow recurrence estimates frequency, and persistent sliding-window geometry describes the rhythmicity of the movement. Across 1,890 synthetic conditions, the measurements recover controlled speed, amplitude, and frequency while exposing observation limits. An idealized hand-motion experiment demonstrates variation omitted by identical exact COCO-17 trajectories; controlled corruption experiments separately examine measurement sensitivity. Audits of two pose methods on the same data cohort and 36,930 external skeleton clips document incomplete observation and dependence on processing choices. In 1,404 annotated complex stereotypical motor movement bouts from six autistic participants, total flow converges with pose motion, while matched-coordinate examples and repeated-session profiles show differences in intensity, extent, frequency, and rhythmicity within behavior labels. A separate VLM comparison evaluates quantitative frequency estimation, and a profile-conditioned decoder links the measurements to illustrative skeletal movements. PRISM connects numerical profiles to visible examples, providing an interpretable way to compare how the same behavior is expressed beyond its label or event count.

papers.title: Theorems of the Alternative and Nonnegativity Certificates for Systems of Jensen-type Polynomials with Universal Quantifiers
papers.abstract: We introduce Jensen-type polynomials, a class of possibly nonconvex polynomials that extends the Jensen inequality for SOS-convex polynomials while retaining natural sums of squares (SOS) certificates for nonnegativity. We show that polynomials with essentially nonpositive coefficients belong to this class and establish a composition principle that yields further examples, including componentwise univariate compositions and compositions with structured quadratic maps motivated by source-localization loss functions. We then derive theorems of the alternative that provide SOS certificates for infeasibility of systems of strict inequalities involving Jensen-type polynomials and universally quantified variables. We illustrate our results through two applications, with numerical examples. First, we show that source-localization problems admit an exact SOS reformulation under a simple dimension condition, and that an optimal solution can be recovered by solving a semidefinite program (SDP) and applying the explicit Jensen map. Second, our SOS certificates yield two {\it convergent} SDP hierarchies for semi-infinite optimization with Jensen-type polynomials, providing upper and lower bounds on the optimal value. We also establish finite-convergence and solution-extraction results, under flat truncation rank condition and the associated Jensen maps.

papers.title: From Persistent Cohomology to Maps into Arbitrary Eilenberg-MacLane Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the construction of Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates (functions from datasets to Eilenberg-MacLane spaces $K(G,n)$) that encode nontrivial persistent cohomology classes in arbitrary dimensions $n$ and coefficient group $G$. The construction leverages the connecting homomorphism in the long exact sequence in \v{C}ech cohomology, from the short exact sequence of sheaves of continuous maps with values in $G$, $EG$ and $BG$. Crucially, the derivation is constructive: we give an explicit, recursive formula for preimages under the connecting homomorphism, which yields a constructive version of a classical cohomology vanishing theorem and, in turn, an algorithm for general Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates. We validate our approach through experiments on synthetic datasets, and present novel examples of $K(\mathbb{Z}/2, 2)$-coordinates not addressed in prior work.

papers.title: A Multisite Super Learner for Survival Prediction with Limited Target-Site Data
papers.abstract: Survival prediction models developed in multi-site studies may transport poorly to a new site because of between-site heterogeneity in covariate effects and baseline hazards. Pooled models may fail to capture site-specific risk patterns, while site-specific models can be unstable in small cohorts. We propose a Multi-Site Super Learner (MSSL), a domain-adaptive ensemble for survival prediction that combines diverse pooled and site-specific base learners. A meta-learner optimizes the ensemble weights using source data alone or, if available, a small target-site calibration sample. In simulations, when even a small target-site sample was available, MSSL substantially reduced prediction error relative to a pooled super learner under moderate to large between-site heterogeneity and generally matched or improved upon models fit to the target-site data alone. It did so by downweighting dissimilar or noisy models and upweighting models from structurally similar sites. Without target-site data, MSSL did not improve upon the pooled super learner. In an application to predicting dementia progression using the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) Uniform Data Set across 10 sites, MSSL matched or outperformed standard super learning using pooled data in 9 of 10 sites. MSSL offers a practical framework for adapting multi-site survival prediction models to a new site when a small calibration sample is available.

papers.title: Authenticating IoT Data on Ethereum after Pectra and Fusaka: A Cost Study of Signature Schemes, Batching and Anchoring for Agricultural Supply Chain Finance
papers.abstract: Blockchain-based supply chain finance can turn the sensor-recorded production history of smallholder farms into verifiable credit evidence, but only if every record is authenticated and anchored at a cost that scales to large device fleets. Ethereum's 2025 Pectra and Fusaka upgrades changed this cost landscape: they added precompiles for BLS12-381 and P-256, repriced calldata and MODEXP, and capped transaction gas at $2^{24}$. We organize the authentication and anchoring of IoT records into three trust levels, from posting a Merkle root through a trusted aggregator to verifying every device signature on-chain, and implement four replay-protected signature designs: ECDSA over secp256k1 and P-256, BLS aggregate signatures with on-chain hash-to-curve, and a pseudonymous identity-based signature with batch verification. Measured as signed transactions under the rules before and after both upgrades, the upgrades mainly changed which designs are feasible, not their cost. Batching and Merkle anchoring cut the cost of ECDSA authentication sixfold, to 8,963 gas per record, and secp256k1 ECDSA remains the cheapest authenticated design: P-256 costs 1.6 times as much, the identity-based design 2.7 times and BLS aggregation 3.9 times, dominated by on-chain hashing to the curve. One transaction carries at most 1,754 ECDSA-authenticated records but only 411 BLS-aggregated ones. On a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, pairing-based signing takes 5.7 ms against 0.29 ms for ECDSA. Pairing-based designs pay off only when the application needs their additional properties, and the identity-based design adds key escrow at the key generation centre. The benchmark harness is released for reproducibility.

authors.name: Gwan-yen Lin
authors.institution: National Taiwan University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yen-Shuo Chen
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: Indecomposable representations of $C^{\infty}(S^1,\aff)$ on polynomial spaces over jet spaces
papers.abstract: We study a class of finite dimensional complex vector spaces \(\pn\), \(n \in \bn\), consisting of polynomials on \(\jnmc\), the space of \((n-1)\) jets at a fixed point \(t_0 \in S^1\) of \(C^\infty\) functions \(S^1 \to \bc\). The loop group \(C^\infty(S^1,\aff)\) of the affine group \(\aff\) acts naturally on \(\pn\) by an indecomposable linear representation. The space \(\pn\) is canonically isomorphic to the space of holomorphic sections of a certain line bundle over the loop space of the Riemann sphere. It has an intricate structure, leading to infinite families of combinatorial identities. In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for a polynomial on \(\jnmc\) to belong to \(\pn\). Furthermore, we give partial answers to several conjectures concerning \(\pn\).

papers.title: Training-Free Domain Generation for One-Shot Federated Learning with Server-Side Pre-trained Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: One-shot federated learning (OSFL) has attracted increasing attention for its ability to substantially reduce communication overhead by limiting client-server interaction to a single communication round. Nevertheless, this limited interaction makes learning from heterogeneous client distributions challenging. Diffusion-based OSFL approaches seek to address this challenge by synthesizing data that approximate client distributions. However, existing diffusion-based approaches often impose substantial computational costs on clients and lack effective visual guidance to generate data aligned with client distributions. To address these limitations, we propose FedDoG, a training-free Domain Generation framework that leverages server-side pre-trained diffusion models to synthesize data aligned with client domains. FedDoG extracts compact domain representations using a frozen image encoder, substantially reducing client-side computational and communication costs. These representations are incorporated into the diffusion model through a pre-trained image-conditioning adapter, thereby providing explicit visual guidance for domain generation. To further improve the quality of synthetic data, FedDoG adapts the strength of visual conditioning according to domain concentration and filters generated samples based on class consistency and predictive entropy. Experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that FedDoG generates higher-quality synthetic images and outperforms existing OSFL baselines in classification accuracy. Meanwhile, FedDoG reduces client upload and computation time by 99.9% and 91.5%, respectively. The code is available at https://github.com/YXTong17/FedDoG.

papers.title: Convolution-Augmented Transformer for Robust Blind CFO Estimation in LEO Satellite Communication System
papers.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communications are essential for achieving ubiquitous global connectivity. However, the high mobility of LEO satellites induces massive Doppler shifts and fast time-varying fading, severely impairing signal synchronization. Accurate Carrier Frequency Offset (CFO) estimation is critical for receiver synchronization. Nevertheless, conventional estimators and deep learning approaches often degrade significantly under highly dynamic, low-SNR conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Convolution Augmented Transformer architecture for robust, blind CFO estimation in LEO communication systems. Initially, to overcome the inherent limitations of standard linear embedding layers in capturing nonlinear phase rotations, we construct a multi-domain input feature that encompasses in-phase/quadrature (I/Q), polar, and statistical autocorrelation properties. Subsequently, a Convolutional Pre-Denoising (CPD) module, integrating multi-scale dilated convolutions and an attention mechanism, is deployed at the front end to adaptively suppress localized noise and extract robust spatiotemporal representations. These refined latent features are then processed by a Transformer encoder to explicitly track global, long-range phase dependencies. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed data-driven approach significantly outperforms conventional estimation algorithms, achieving enhanced estimation accuracy and superior resilience in highly dynamic LEO environments.

authors.name: Miaomiao Wei
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
papers.abstract: Frontier post-training follows a common recipe: train one expert per domain with reinforcement learning (RL), then consolidate the experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Such consolidation is expensive: the student samples in every environment again, an expert scores every sampled token, and the student inherits the drift of the final experts. Yet we argue that the experts' RL runs have already produced what consolidation needs: rollouts with their sampling probabilities and rewards, in the order the experts learned from them. We propose multi-expert replay policy distillation (MRPD), which replays these training logs through the student in the experts' order. At each step, the policy gradient is recomputed on these scored trajectories, and the final experts' distributions are distilled at the logged prefixes. Following the experts' own trajectory reduces the training-inference mismatch and keeps the student within the clip range, so the replay is off-policy in origin but quasi-on-policy throughout consolidation. MRPD samples nothing and calls no environment or reward model: the trainer is the sole process, and consolidating the experts costs only about a seventh of the compute used to train them. On three long-horizon agentic domains (reasoning, search and SQL), MRPD yields the best student model, substantially outperforming online RL baselines, and surpassing MOPD from the same experts at a fraction of MOPD's cost. Our analysis on the same logs shows that the replayed trajectories carry most of the gain, and that both the policy gradient and the distillation term add to it. Most interestingly, the order of the logs matters more than their amount or rewards, suggesting that expert training logs are a curriculum, not a data mixture.

authors.name: Jiashuo Sun
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: R$^{3}$Sieve: Suppressing Unconditional Information from Attention to Answers for High-Resolution VQA
papers.abstract: High-resolution visual question answering (VQA) requires models to identify question-relevant small objects in high-resolution images and select the correct answer based on what they recognize, demanding fine-grained perception. Previous methods focus on obtaining better visual evidence (image crops), but obtaining it alone is insufficient, using it effectively is equally crucial. Visual evidence should therefore be utilized as effectively as possible throughout inference. We argue that small-target evidence is obscured by unconditional information that remains observable in subsequent processing even after the condition on which it should depend is removed. Such information hinders the effective use of small-target evidence. We propose R$^{3}$Sieve (Residual-Region-Response Sieve), a training-free framework. We divide inference into three stages---localization, cropping, and answering---and introduce distinct counterfactual references to suppress interference at each stage. During localization, the Shared-Subspace Canceller (SSC) uses a generic image description to construct a counterfactual reference and obtain question-relevant attention maps. During cropping, the Unique-Contribution Spotter (UCS) constructs counterfactual references from visual and non-visual features to identify distinctive, complementary crop regions. During answering, the Content-Aligned Voter (CAV) constructs an image-free branch to calibrate answer responses. Experiments on three high-resolution VQA benchmarks show that R$^{3}$Sieve achieves the highest overall accuracy among compared methods across diverse settings, improving base models by up to 21.5 percentage points.

authors.name: Yawen Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Euclidean Quasi-Newton Method for Matrix-Manifold Optimization via Almost-Global Coordinates
papers.abstract: We study smooth matrix-manifold optimization using objective values and first derivatives. Almost-global coordinates transform the manifold-constrained problem into an unconstrained pullback problem, to which we apply BFGS with a chart-restart strategy and a limited-memory implementation. We establish correspondence of first- and second-order stationary points and minimizers, together with conditional convergence and local q-superlinear convergence. The local rate follows from Euclidean full-memory BFGS theory once the chart is fixed, without the locking condition required by classical transported-gradient Riemannian BFGS analyses. Tests on 15 benchmark problems from Manopt and Pymanopt, with ten instances per problem, show that our limited-memory method solves all 150 cases, whereas Riemannian BFGS and Riemannian steepest descent solve 132 and 117 cases, respectively. On the 115 cases successfully solved by all three methods, our method takes roughly half the time of either baseline, measured by geometric-mean solve time.

papers.title: SCOPE: Single-Cell Omics Prediction from Histology via RNA-Protein Prior Enhancement
papers.abstract: Predicting the RNA and protein content of cells from routine H&E images could extend spatial molecular profiling to existing slide archives. However, both H&E-spatial proteomics and H&E-spatial transcriptomics paired datasets are limited by the number of available markers and the insufficient availability of high-quality, cell-resolved data. We present SCOPE (Single-Cell Omics Prediction via RNA-protein prior Enhancement), a unified framework that leverages biologically complementary information between RNA and proteins to address the limited availability of single-omics supervision. Our key insight is that, although RNA and proteins represent distinct molecular modalities, their biological relationships provide valuable shared knowledge that can benefit single-omics prediction tasks. To this end, SCOPE introduces biologically informed biomarker priors to enhance shared gene-level representations, enabling knowledge transfer across RNA and protein modalities through gene-protein correspondence and molecular associations. By exploiting these complementary relationships, SCOPE enables both prediction tasks to benefit from a shared backbone enriched with cross-omics biological knowledge. Furthermore, its biomarker correlation design facilitates the prediction of unseen markers, extending spatially resolved molecular profiling beyond directly supervised targets. Across test datasets spanning 16 organs, SCOPE improves the average RNA Pearson correlation over the strongest baseline by 8.8%. On two external protein cohorts, it improves the average Pearson correlation over the strongest baseline by 9.7% for seen markers and 11.9% for unseen markers.

authors.name: Leyang Tao
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Oncogene and Related Genes

papers.title: EVF-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for E-commerce Visual Effects in Video Generation
papers.abstract: E-commerce visual effects (EVF) are dynamic, product-centered visual presentations in e-commerce videos, often accompanied by promotional text. They play an important role in attracting viewer attention and conveying product information. However, general measures of visual quality and text relevance alone do not establish whether generated videos preserve product appearance, maintain readable text, and produce coherent, contextually appropriate effects. To address this issue, we introduce EVF-Bench, a dedicated benchmark spanning six evaluation dimensions: visual quality and text relevance as general dimensions, and motion, product consistency, text stability, and creative rationality as EVF-specific dimensions. To complement the benchmark and support task-aligned research and model adaptation, we further construct EVF-32K, a dataset of over 32000 curated image-text-video triples tailored to e-commerce scenarios. Using this suite, we systematically evaluate representative video generation models and their domain-adapted variants. The results reveal complementary strengths, with no evaluated configuration leading all six dimensions. Together, EVF-Bench and EVF-32K provide a task-oriented evaluation framework and a supporting data resource for e-commerce video generation.

papers.title: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents
papers.abstract: Multimodal language models increasingly answer questions over external documents, exposing them to indirect prompt injection: commands planted in untrusted content to hijack the response. Rendering untrusted content as page images lowers attack success on average, leaving open which injected operations survive rendering, at what utility cost, and whether failed image attacks reflect unread commands or commands read but not followed. We pair text and page-image versions of 191 English question-answering sources across six models, measuring marker appending, answer formatting, and answer replacement alongside clean Question-Answering utility. Rendering reduces append and format execution for every model, yet Qwen3-VL-8B still executes image-borne replacement at 77.96\%. Protection also depends on target type, rendering settings, wording, and repetition, and a search over eight fixed attack candidates largely closes the image deficit in appending and formatting for Qwen and Gemini, though not for GPT-5-nano. Utility ratios on original questions range from 93.31\% to 101.61\%, but Qwen falls to 61.99\% when answers combine two evidence spans. Illegibility cannot explain all failed attacks: models often transcribe and identify image-borne commands they do not execute, and trusted user authorization raises execution on unchanged pages. Inside Qwen, patching early attack-region states induces all three operations, more weakly in images. Attention blocking suggests why: a text command acts through its own positions, whereas visual encoding spreads an image command and its target across the instruction page. Rendering thus offers conditional protection, motivating evaluations that report security by model, operation, and attack budget alongside utility.

papers.title: One Affinity, Two Axes: Bidirectional Slot Attention for Iterative Aggregation across the Structure--Detail Spectrum in Visual Retrieval
papers.abstract: Aggregating dense patch tokens into compact and discriminative global descriptors is central to visual retrieval. Although foundation models provide rich local features, existing aggregation heads still rely on single-pass mappings and lack an explicit mechanism to coordinate structural and fine-grained cues. Therefore, we propose Bidirectional Slot Attention (BiSA), which reformulates aggregation as an iterative coupled system. Cross-Axis Consensus (CAC) progressively refines learnable slots by interpreting a single shared token--slot affinity along two complementary axes. Along the competition axis, slots vie for each token under a temperature shared across all of them, determining token ownership and inducing a non-redundant scene decomposition. Along the selection axis, a slot-specific temperature governs the breadth of each slot's response, spanning a spectrum from broad layouts to sparse fine-grained details. Their consensus couples non-redundant decomposition with multi-granular slot specialization. Furthermore, the two axes expose intrinsic token-reliability cues at no extra cost: a token's claim strength under competition and its salience under selection. Progressive Token Filtering (PTF) converts these cues into a retention probability that down-weights unreliable tokens before the next CAC iteration, without any segmentation branch or external prior, forming a self-reinforcing loop of competitive decomposition, selective focusing, and feedback purification. Across all three retrieval tasks, BiSA leads on five of six place recognition benchmarks (+4.2 R@1 on Baidu Mall), tops all 16 metrics of drone--satellite geo-localization (+8.4 R@1 at 150 m), and improves instance-level retrieval on ROxford-Hard by 4.5 mAP points. Notably, the selection axis adds only 20 learnable scalars, yet improves average R@1 by 2.8 points.

papers.title: LLM-Assisted Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization: Fusing Expert Knowledge with Numerical Data
papers.abstract: Multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization (MFBO) reduces engineering design cost by combining inexpensive low-fidelity (LF) models with a few accurate high-fidelity (HF) evaluations and sequentially selecting designs to evaluate. However, when HF data are scarce, the LF-HF discrepancy is difficult to learn from numerical data alone, especially when physics omitted in the LF model makes it design-dependent. Yet even without sufficient data, domain experts often know which physics the LF model omits and under which conditions its effect grows. Existing multi-fidelity (MF) models cannot use such qualitative knowledge directly, but large language models (LLMs) can interpret it and compare designs accordingly. The proposed LLM-Assisted MFBO adds a knowledge basis to the conventional MF model: from an expert description of the omitted physics, an LLM judges which of two designs requires the larger signed residual correction, and a pairwise Gaussian process converts these judgments into the basis. HF data calibrate its contribution and sign, so the knowledge is not trusted blindly. On a lithium-ion battery design problem, the proposed method reduced the regret area under the curve of conventional MFBO by 61%. Knowledge quality, rather than the choice of LLM, determined whether the search was accelerated, as shown by a controlled study that varied the two independently. A knowledge-level ablation further quantified the contribution of each knowledge statement. These results show that LLM-interpreted expert knowledge can complement numerical data as an information source in MFBO.

authors.name: Mingyu Lee
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Ikjin Lee
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\Cs$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.

papers.title: Interpretable attention-based neural posterior estimation for fast radio burst cosmology
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe the integrated free-electron density along extragalactic sightlines and can be used to study late-time cosmic evolution. Conventional Bayesian analyses require repeated evaluations of computationally expensive likelihoods, making inference increasingly challenging as FRB catalogs grow. In this work, we develop an interpretable attention-based neural posterior estimator (AttNPE) for rapid posterior inference of the physical parameters from FRB catalogs with measured redshifts. The attention encoder compresses the catalog into a low-dimensional representation, and a conditional masked autoregressive flow maps samples from a base distribution to the seven-dimensional posterior. AttNPE yields posterior distributions in close agreement with Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), recovering the parameter correlations in both simulated and observed FRB catalogs. For the observed catalog, AttNPE generates $5\times10^4$ posterior samples in $0.036$~s after training, compared with $72.8$~h for the reference MCMC run, giving an elapsed-time ratio of $O(10^6)$. The attention-weight analysis shows that intermediate-redshift FRBs ($0.3\leq z<0.7$) account for the largest share of the total attention averaged over simulated catalogs following the observed redshift distribution, consistent with the combined influence of source abundance and redshift-dependent sensitivity. These results demonstrate the potential of interpretable neural posterior estimation for efficient and repeated inference in FRB cosmology.

authors.name: Tian-Yang Sun
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Slope stability for normal varieties
papers.abstract: In this expository paper, we review the theory of slope stability of torsion-free sheaves with respect to nef curve classes and extend it to normal varieties.

papers.title: Grain-size distribution characterization from single-shot x-ray diffraction using hierarchical Bayesian multi-emitter analysis
papers.abstract:
The distribution of grain sizes in a polycrystalline material can be determined from a 2D x-ray diffraction pattern by counting and characterizing diffraction spots, so long as the spots are discrete. This approach breaks down if there is substantial overlap of the reflections due to either a large number of grains in the scattering volume or crowding of spots caused by crystallographic texture. As a result, the spot-counting approach to grain size determination is infeasible for many situations of practical interest.
  We address this limitation by applying hierarchical probabilistic learning using a reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo framework to jointly infer diffraction spot populations and their intensity distributions. Using synthetic diffraction patterns, we show how this hierarchical model allows recovery of diffraction peak intensities across a wide variety of grain-size distributions and crystallographic textures. From the recovered peak intensities we infer grain-size distributions themselves and characterize the regimes of grain size and texture for which this approach is practical. Finally, we demonstrate the application of our technique by comparing grain-size distributions in Cu-Ti alloy specimens obtained from 2D x-ray diffraction patterns with those from electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). This method of grain-size distribution determination is expected to be particularly useful in the context of high-throughput experimentation, where the minimal sample preparation requirements and short exposure times of single-shot x-ray diffraction are substantial advantages relative to microscopy techniques.

papers.title: Kaer: Security-Aware Replanning for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract:
One popular architecture for multi-agent systems (MAS) relies on an orchestrator that generates an initial plan, coordinates its execution, and dynamically revises the plan based on agent feedback when tasks cannot be fully specified in advance. This dynamic replanning introduces a critical vulnerability: malicious agents can embed instructions within their feedback to hijack the replanning process. Existing defenses focus exclusively on per-tool access control or static, pre-execution policy enforcement, leaving the replanning phase unsecured.
  We introduce Kaer, a multi-agent framework featuring security-aware replanning. Kaer shields the planner from untrusted agent feedback by conveying diagnostics to the replanning procedure strictly through abstract templates. Plan revisions are restricted to a set of deterministic repair operators, and all modified plans must satisfy preset policies. We create Cintra, a benchmark of simulated user tasks requiring replanning paired with adversarial objectives targeting the replanning phase. Using Cintra, we evaluate both task completion rates and system vulnerability to replanning exploits by malicious agents. Evaluating Kaer on Cintra against Magentic-One (an undefended MAS) and ControlValve (the state-of-the-art defense) demonstrates that Kaer achieves higher robustness than both systems while maintaining comparable utility to ControlValve. Although abstract failure templates slightly constrain utility on select tasks, Kaer enables MAS to perform secure, dynamic plan revisions without exposing the orchestrator to untrusted agent feedback.

papers.title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
papers.abstract: For $\kappa\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_\kappa$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circ\psi^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a relative action well defined for SLE weldings and prove that it belongs to $L^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending on the pair.

papers.title: Monoculture Robust Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of monoculture robustness in Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning, as a way to mitigate the problem of algorithmic monoculture (Kleinberg and Raghavan, 2021): the tendency of models sharing the same components (e.g., training data) to fail on the same inputs. Specifically, we ask whether a learner with access to a single dataset can output $k$ individually accurate hypotheses whose joint failure probability is comparable to training on $k$ independent datasets. We say that such a learning procedure achieves monoculture robustness, and we quantify this by bounding the conjunctive error that all $k$ hypotheses misclassify points in an individual sense. We design methods for achieving this type of guarantee by drawing a surprising connection between replicability (Impagliazzo et al., 2022) and monoculture robustness. Specifically, we show that if the base learner is $\rho$-replicable, then running it independently $k$ times on the same sample yields individual monoculture error that shrinks exponentially with $k$, controlled by the single-run error of the base learner at the point and $\rho$. We complement these positive results with a lower bound: for individual monoculture robustness, we prove a worst-case lower bound showing that, for learners, driving the individual conjunctive error down to $\gamma$ can require a sample-size multiplier of $t = \Omega(\log(1/\gamma))$.

papers.title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity
papers.abstract: A fixed dispatch rate for LLM inference becomes stale as serving fleets resize and request sizes change. Generative output length is unknown at admission, and shared provider pools can lose capacity. We present Cap-and-Track, a design for asynchronous inference across provider capacity and internal GPUs. Meta's traffic shaper implements Cap-and-Track for post and live-video understanding. Refusals signal the backend's current admission ceiling. Durable priority queues hold excess work outside execution, including refused requests for retry. Cap is a fail-fast admission check at the saturated resource that refuses work before a long wait. Using only those refusals, the Track dispatcher probes upward and backs off. It follows the ceiling without output-length prediction or a fleet-level rate to retune. In a concurrent same-traffic production A/B, the shaper ran per-replica Cap plus Track. It served a classifier on 43% fewer H100s than its queued, fixed-rate precursor, though lower-priority work waited longer at backfill peaks. In steady-capacity real-engine replay, Track ran within 1% of the goodput of a fixed rate tuned above measured capacity, with about a quarter of that rate's refusal share. The shaper carries more than 300 million online requests and hundreds of terabytes of media a day. During a backfill, it handled 1.1 billion requests in its busiest 24 hours. Lessons include keeping queues inside inference engines just long enough to fill batches, steering dispatch by capacity refusals alone, keeping dispatch stateful, and sizing fleets by how long low-priority work can wait.

papers.title: "I Don't Think It's a Scam": A First Look at Family Intervention Barriers in Elder Abuse Discussions on Reddit and Baidu Tieba
papers.abstract: When older adults trust scammers despite warnings, families face obstacles to intervention. Complainants aged 60 and older reported \$4.9 billion in losses in 2024 to the U.S. Internet Crime Complaint Center. To investigate family intervention barriers to elder scams, we collected 2M Reddit posts from May 2021 to June 2026 and 2B Baidu Tieba posts from 2007 to 2026. The final corpora contain 13,082 Reddit posts and 3,933 Baidu Tieba posts, labeled using platform-specific codebooks, manual reference annotations, and LLM coding. Through a mixed-methods analysis, we find that scams often extend beyond a single incident and are reported alongside debt problems and broken family relationships. In 68.0\% of Reddit posts recording reactions, older adults showed resistance or continued involvement; in Baidu Tieba family-confrontation posts, 41.9\% showed continued belief. Relatives identified fraud in 74.4\% of Reddit posts and narrated cases on Baidu Tieba, but without the victim's consent, relatives may lack the legal authority to intervene. In Reddit posts recording reactions, account locks or credential changes appeared in 8.9\% under resistance or continued involvement, compared with 33.3\% under acceptance. Measures such as phone or network monitoring and financial takeover were reported more often under resistance. Recovering funds is very limited in posts recording follow-up results of fraud; Baidu Tieba users reported that police classified older adults' voluntary transfers as civil disputes.

authors.name: Yipeng Wang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Mihika Mehta
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Arlington

authors.name: Poojitha Thota
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Arlington

authors.name: Shirin Nilizadeh

papers.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
papers.abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We implement this by adding a separate, third-person observer role that answers these queries, which we can train solely for accuracy and separately from the assistant. On five held-out oversight evaluations, an observer trained on Qwen3.6-27B obtains a mean AUROC of 0.907, outperforming honesty training (0.864), transcript monitoring (0.828), and activation oracles (0.796). We further find that training an observer makes the assistant itself easier to monitor, with every baseline method improving on average when applied to the fine-tuned assistant. These results suggest that training models to answer verifiable questions about themselves is a tractable approach to overseeing unintended behavior.

papers.title: Error accumulation in reverse diffusion with an imperfect score: beyond path-space analyses
papers.abstract:
Diffusion modeling is a popular method of sampling from a complex, high-dimensional distribution $p$ using learned approximations of its (noised) score functions. Generating a single sample requires simulating the reverse diffusion process, which requires many queries to the learned scores. Thus, a priori, the learning errors can easily compound. Indeed, in existing theoretical analyses, the sampling error (as measured in total variation distance to $p$) accumulates polynomially with the horizon of the stochastic process. This is a consequence of bounding the error of the output law by the error of the law of the entire reverse diffusion path.
  In this paper, we demonstrate that by circumventing the "path-space" analysis, the error accumulation of the diffusion sampler can be mitigated when $p$ satisfies a Poincar\'e inequality. Moreover, we achieve this result as a special case of a broader framework that applies to any distribution $p$, but relaxes the error metric from total variation distance to a weaker metric capturing all sample statistics that do not "witness" the multimodality of $p$.
  We then zoom out from analyzing the diffusion sampler to the information-theoretic question: given a learned score with some error bound, how accurately can we identify $p$? We show that, for any given bound on the Poincar\'e constant of $p$, the diffusion sampler already nearly achieves optimal total variation error.

papers.title: Miscalibrated AI improves human calibration: An alignment problem for AI-assisted Decision education
papers.abstract: Using artificial intelligence (AI) well requires probabilistic thinking, and central to it is calibration: expressing certainty that matches one's actual accuracy. Calibration is a decision skill, but a notoriously difficult one to teach. Because AI systems typically generate a probability alongside every prediction, observing these probabilities may help humans learn to provide better calibrated judgments. This is one form of what we call AI-assisted decision education -- using AI to teach the judgment skills that decision-making requires -- of which learning by observation, as here, is among the simplest forms. In a preregistered experiment, novice participants (N = 300) judged the probability that images of white blood cells were cancerous, before and after exposure to a highly accurate (94%) convolutional neural network. A single model was shown in three ways, holding accuracy fixed while varying the certainty it expressed: its original probabilities, which were conservative and poorly calibrated for the model's accuracy; a recalibrated version, well calibrated for the model and correspondingly certain; or categorical predictions carrying no probability information. When later tested without the AI, only the original, conservative display improved participants' calibration. It did so by reducing over-extremity, without a condition-specific improvement in discrimination. Notably, the display that taught best was the one miscalibrated for the model. AI-assisted decision education therefore faces an alignment problem: the signal that best describes a model, need not be the signal that best supports the learner.

authors.name: Phillip C. Hegeman
authors.institution: National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities

papers.title: Benchmarking Linux CGroup and Schedule Idle
papers.abstract: cgroups are a Linux kernel primitive that limits, accounts for, and isolates the resource usage (CPU, memory, disk I/O) of a collection of processes. Many provider-side serverless systems (Mitosis, gVisor, Havest VM, FAASM) leverage linux containers based around cgroups/namespaces for their performance isolation. However, how well does this primitive map to the needs of serverless platforms? How does the linux CFS scheduler deal with cgroups and SCHED IDLE and what are the core sources of high tail latency? Would a new primitive design fit the needs of serverless isolation better? In this work we take the first step to answering these questions by profiling the current behavior of cgroups and a sched idle policy via a thorough benchmarking study. We emulate the setting of Performance-Critical (LC) server in the presence of an intensive background (BE) process and note the impact of each primitive on the performance of the server. We show it is non-trivial to balance the potential tail-latency impact on a LC server with the throughput of BE tasks. Furthermore, there are many variables to adjust for the developer between hard maximum bandwidth limits, weighted cpu shares, the presence of the sched idle policy, or additionally "niceness" priority in the scheduling policy.

papers.title: Toward Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Neural AC Power Flow
papers.abstract: Growing uncertainty in power system operations from renewables integration, extreme weather, and data center loads challenges the reliability of traditional power flow solvers at scale. Machine learning-based proxies are a potentially promising alternative, but the prohibitive cost of generating training data for large grids makes out-of-distribution generalization a key capability for deployment; currently, models trained on small grids lack that capability. In this work, we systematically evaluate how physics-informed losses, multi-grid training, and perturbation-based data augmentation improve the zero-shot transfer of three graph neural network-based power flow models from smaller systems to a larger, unseen 500-bus system. We find that (1) physics-informed losses improve transfer relative to purely supervised objectives; (2) multi-grid training on smaller systems matches the best single grid but does not close the gap to target-grid training; (3) perturbation-based augmentation on edge attributes improves transfer by up to 54.6%; and (4) random line/generator dropout does not consistently improve performance.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic limit of the Toda lattice
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the Toda lattice under random, spatially inhomogeneous initial data, meaning that its initial momenta and interparticle spacings are independent and their laws may slowly vary in space. When the density is strictly positive (but sufficiently small), we identify the model's hydrodynamic limit under Euler scaling. More precisely, we prove that spatial averages of each of the model's local conserved quantities converge to moments of a density $m_{\tau}(\lambda,q)$ solving the generalized hydrodynamic equation predicted by Doyon arXiv:1902.07624 and Spohn arXiv:1902.07751. To do so, we justify the notion that the Toda lattice can be thought of as a dense collection of many "quasiparticles" that interact through scattering. As in Aggarwal arXiv:2503.08018, we define these quasiparticles through spectral properties of the Toda Lax matrix, but in our inhomogeneous setting we must now show that the eigenvectors of this Lax matrix remain localized throughout the dynamics. The core of our work is to show that, with high probability, the quasiparticle trajectories converge to the characteristic curves of the generalized hydrodynamic equation.

papers.title: RoboBuilder: Agentic Robot Co-Design with Real-world Video Feedback in the Loop
papers.abstract: Can AI agents design robots that work in the real world? We introduce RoboBuilder, a benchmark in which coding agents co-design a robot's hardware and program from standard parts, motors and a custom 3D-printed part, and every design that passes in simulation is built and tested on a physical course. Simulation alone is not enough: under public part data, none of 15 initial passing designs crossed the real course, so an agent learns the simulator from measurements it requests and videos of real runs. Across four frontier coding agents, ten obstacles at three difficulty levels, 16,427 simulations of 12,774 distinct robots and 135 physical robots built in an estimated 240 hours, agents solve nearly all easy obstacles and invent mechanisms our search baselines do not reach, but falter at harder levels, when one robot must cross every obstacle, and in the real world, where 66% of simulated passes hold across all levels. Closing the loop helps: shown a video of its real failure, an agent redesigns the robot, sometimes correcting its simulator, and removes 72% of level-1 and level-2 failures. RoboBuilder measures progress toward agents that engineer real machines. Project Page: https://ghadinehme.com/robobuilder.github.io/

papers.title: Technical Note on Matlantis PFP v9: Extending the Element and Domain Coverage of the r2SCAN Training Data
papers.abstract: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) make atomistic simulations possible at scales beyond the reach of density functional theory (DFT). Matlantis PFP is a uMLIP that treats a variety of domains, including crystals, molecules, and surfaces, with a single model. PFP v8 incorporated a training dataset computed with the r2SCAN functional, chosen for its good agreement with experiment, but the elements and domains covered by that dataset were limited. Here we present Matlantis PFP v9, in which the training data computed with the r2SCAN functional are extended to the lanthanides from Pr to Lu and to the elements from Po to Cm, for a total of 96 elements, and to additional domains such as clusters and adsorption structures. The formation energies of crystals containing the newly supported elements reproduce experimental standard enthalpies of formation with the same level of accuracy as crystals composed only of previously supported elements, and the adsorption energies of molecules on transition-metal surfaces have an overall error against experiment comparable to that of DFT-PBE, although chemisorbed species are overbound. On the same type of GPU (A100), the inference speed and the maximum system size exceed those of SevenNet-Omni, a public uMLIP trained on r2SCAN data: forces are evaluated three to four times faster, and five to ten times as many atoms can be handled. As a result, PFP-R2SCAN is now applicable to systems containing rare-earth and actinide elements and to adsorption on surfaces.

papers.title: TRoPE: Topology-aware Relative Positional Encoding for 4D Generation
papers.abstract: Video-to-4D mesh generation has made substantial progress in recovering dynamic 3D geometry and motion from monocular videos. However, commonly used feed-forward approaches remain prone to sticking artifacts, where geodesically distant vertices move together incorrectly when they become spatially close. We attribute this failure to cross-part motion leakage: spatially nearby yet structurally distant vertices may retrieve similar motion information when motion decoding fails to distinguish spatial proximity from mesh connectivity. To address this issue, we introduce TRoPE, a topology-aware relative positional encoding that makes mesh connectivity explicit in the interaction between vertex queries and mesh-supported motion sources. TRoPE derives spectral features from the graph Laplacian and constructs pairwise topological relations from distances between multi-scale diffusion features, using these relations to modulate vertex--anchor attention through rotary phases. We further introduce a vertex-wise tail-risk objective that emphasizes persistently high-error vertices to explicitly suppress sticking artifacts. To better characterize and quantify these failures, we introduce MeshSticking-4D, a dedicated benchmark for this failure mode. Experiments on MeshSticking-4D show that TRoPE suppresses sticking artifacts while improving overall motion accuracy. Compared with the baseline, it reduces the worst-vertex error by 39.4% and lowers the separation failure rate from 49.35% to 34.90%. Additional evaluations on Motion-80 and Motion324-Subset show lower tail errors on diverse objects, while transfer to Mesh4D demonstrates applicability across backbones.

papers.title: ReCIM-HD: A 40 nm On-Device Learning Accelerator with Hyperdimensional Computing via Importance-Based Hybrid Digital-ReRAM CIM
papers.abstract: ReCIM-HD is an on-device learning (ODL) accelerator that integrates gradient-free hyperdimensional computing (HDC) with resistive RAM (ReRAM)-based analog compute-in-memory (CIM). ReCIM-HD introduces three key techniques: (1) ultra-low-power HDC-based edge ODL without costly back-propagation operations; (2) non-volatile ReRAM-based storage for class hypervectors and CIM similarity search, enabling energy-efficient inference and power-gating during idle periods without data loss; and (3) a hybrid digital-analog CIM inference flow that protects a small accuracy-critical subset digitally to preserve accuracy. Additionally, it employs a Kronecker HD encoder (KE) to reduce encoding overhead and a customized instruction set architecture (ISA) to support flexible programmability. Fabricated in 40 nm, ReCIM-HD achieves 44.17 TOPS/W (hybrid mode) and 75.8 TOPS/W (ReRAM CIM mode), delivering up to 20.1x higher energy efficiency than the state-of-the-art accelerator.

authors.name: Chang Eun Song
authors.institution: Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology

papers.title: Test-Time Symmetrization: Scaling Laws for Model-Agnostic Learning under Structure
papers.abstract: Test-time compute has emerged as a powerful way to improve the accuracy of language models at inference time, with scaling laws quantifying how accuracy improves with additional forward passes. Existing scaling laws, however, focus on repeated sampling from a fixed prompt, even though many tasks admit multiple equivalent representations of the same underlying problem. A graph does not depend on how its nodes are numbered, and a program does not depend on the names of its variables, yet language models can change their answers under such rewritings. In this paper, we study test-time symmetrization, which uses forward passes on rewritings of the input and aggregates the resulting answers over the group $G$ of rewritings. We prove that no amount of sampling and repeated decoding from a single representation can replace rewriting, while only $O(\log |G|)$ random rewritings suffice to recover the information provided by all $|G|$ rewritings. The same set of $O(\log |G|)$ rewritings provides simultaneous approximation across models, decoding rules, and sampled reasoning traces, and the logarithmic scaling is optimal in general. We validate the theory with experiments on Qwen2.5-7B, Phi-4-mini, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-14B, with chain-of-thought reasoning, on graph reasoning, logical deduction, and multiple-choice question answering. At the same number of forward passes, spending them on rewritings of the input is substantially more accurate than spending them on repeated sampling from the original prompt whenever the model's answer depends on how the input is written, and the number of rewritings needed grows only logarithmically with the number of possible rewritings, as the theory predicts. Our results provide a principled way to enforce symmetries at inference time when they cannot be built into the model, which we call model-agnostic symmetrization.

papers.title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation
papers.abstract: World models support autonomous driving by evaluating candidate trajectories through predicted future scene evolution. However, accurate future prediction does not ensure road-compliant execution; when all candidates violate road boundaries, re-ranking cannot select a feasible trajectory. We propose Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD), a single-view planning framework that combines future representations and execution feedback for verified beyond-pool repair through three components: (1) Execution-Aware Selection checks ego-vehicle road compliance under simulated execution and selects the highest-scoring feasible trajectory; (2) a Clearance-Aware Search Teacher generates beyond-pool corrections and selects demonstrations with larger minimum road-boundary clearance during execution to buffer imitation errors; and (3) a Future-Conditioned Repair Student predicts one correction from rewarder features and execution feedback for single-rollout verification. The pretrained planner and rewarder remain frozen; no future scenes are generated online. On NAVSIM v1, single-view PGSD achieves 90.97 PDMS, exceeding all compared prior single-view planners and retaining 73.2% of the search teacher's PDMS gain over execution-aware selection. On NAVSIM v2 navhard, it reaches 38.96 EPDMS, improving on WorldDrive by 11.24 points (40.5%). The student replaces up to ten search rollouts with a single verification rollout per repair trigger. HUGSIM Hard examples provide qualitative evidence of zero-shot transfer.

authors.name: Jingyi Zhang
authors.institution: Inner Mongolia University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Multilevel Graph Partitioning on GPU Supercomputers
papers.abstract: Graph partitioning is a key enabler in computational science, with applications to sparse linear algebra, load-balanced parallel computation, and graph computations. In recent years, graphics processing units (GPUs) have become the preferred accelerator on the world's top supercomputers. Despite this, most existing distributed graph partitioners do not utilize GPUs. In this work, we develop a new multi-GPU distributed partitioner based on Jet, a prior single-GPU partitioner. We seek to optimize scalability without sacrificing quality. Our partitioner utilizes CUDA-aware MPI, one-sided communication routines, and an overall bulk-synchronous parallel structure. We demonstrate solution quality comparable to Jet. Our experiments show excellent weak scaling up to 256 GPUs, enabling partitioning of instances significantly larger than a single-GPU partitioner can handle.

papers.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
papers.abstract: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

papers.title: Electrostatic interactions drive the self-assembly of secondary coat-protein layers around wild-type MS2 particles
papers.abstract: The protein capsids of many icosahedral RNA viruses can self-assemble in vitro in the absence of any host cell factors. For bacteriophage MS2 and related viruses, previous studies have focused on the role of specific RNA-protein interactions in driving the assembly process. However, the contribution of electrostatics remains unclear. We show that MS2 coat protein dimers can assemble into additional capsid layers around intact wild-type MS2 particles, even in the absence of free RNA. We characterize the size and morphology of the particles through transmission electron microscopy, gel electrophoresis, and dynamic light scattering, and we use binding and infectivity assays to determine how the maturation protein affects layer formation. Our results are consistent with a heterogeneous nucleation-and-growth assembly pathway, in which the nucleation barrier is controlled by the protein concentration, and electrostatic attraction between the positively charged coat proteins and negatively charged capsid drives growth. Interestingly, the secondary layers rarely fully encapsulate the wild-type particles, suggesting that elastic energy may limit their growth. These results highlight the importance of electrostatics in the assembly of protein shells, even in systems such as MS2 that are known for their strong, specific RNA-protein interactions.

papers.title: BaseRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of a Base Vision-Language Model via Training-Free Harness Internalization
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is moving from the harness of prompts and tools around a base model toward the model itself. However, existing RSI still faces key challenges, including harness-bound gains that stay outside the base model, black-box supervision that reads only the model's outputs, and imprecise edits whose site and strength are fixed in advance. To address these challenges, we propose BaseRSI, a new paradigm of Recursive Harness Internalization: the base model improves its harness, then writes what the harness adds into its own weights through training-free edits, round after round on its own responses. To support this paradigm, we introduce ReGap, a mechanism that supervises every transformer block with the high-dimensional activation difference that the harness makes at that block alone, and updates the block's weights along this signal in a low-dimensional subspace. Building on this mechanism, we further propose ReKey, an algorithm that writes this signal by regression into a few key-value neurons of every block, and measures the site and strength of each edit on the model's own responses. Moreover, the base model fills every role of this recursion with forward passes alone, and its edits, written at different sites, compose in one checkpoint without refitting. Experimental results on ten visual reasoning benchmarks show that BaseRSI consistently improves a base vision-language model both in distribution and on held-out benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/BaseRSI.

authors.name: Mingda Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
papers.abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

papers.title: EgoJev: Finding Evidence in Egocentric Video by Reading VLM Decisions
papers.abstract: Questions about long egocentric video often depend on one brief moment, such as the second a hand puts an object down. A vision-language model (VLM) that sees a few evenly spaced frames usually misses it. Training-free methods rank frames with a separate image-text model or ask the VLM to write a time. In a controlled test, the VLM itself locates the moment better when it chooses among labeled frames, and we read this choice from its output distribution. With the same candidates, this choice lands on the evidence more often than image-text scores or a written time span, and it compares all candidates in one decision. Based on this finding, we propose EgoJev, a training-free frame selector for wearable assistants. EgoJev reads where the evidence is from labeled thumbnails and looks again at the windows it points to. It places its few answer frames at the quantiles of the resulting distribution. One frozen VLM selects, answers and returns the evidence time, with no second model. A wearable device can encode its coarse thumbnails while it records. With Qwen3.5-4B and 8 answer frames, EgoJev raises QAEgo4D accuracy from 51.2% with uniform sampling to 62.0%, and it outperforms recent training-free frame selectors on QAEgo4D and MyEgo. A single-level version runs on a Mac and an iPhone.

papers.title: DrawScore: Evaluating Generated CAD Models against Engineering Drawings
papers.abstract: Automatic CAD generation is commonly evaluated with volumetric IoU, Chamfer Distance, and surface F-score, which barely penalize local errors that occupy only a small fraction of a part's volume or surface area, such as a misplaced hole or a slot on the wrong face, even though such errors are critical to manufacturing. We formalize these metrics in a unified integral form and show that the weight of a local error decays as the $(k+q)$-th power of its size, where $k$ is the dimension of the integration domain and $q$ is determined by the penalty function. Guided by this analysis, we propose DrawScore, which projects both models into three orthographic views with visible and hidden lines, as in engineering drawings, and applies a saturating penalty along the projected curves, so that the weight of a local error decays only linearly. Controlled experiments confirm the predicted decay orders, and on outputs of existing CAD generation agents, DrawScore exposes errors in outputs that IoU rates as nearly perfect. DrawScore further improves generation as a reinforcement learning reward and, for CAD generation from engineering drawings, serves as a test-time verifier without 3D ground truth or an additional reward model. Our code is available at https://github.com/UESTC-Simon/DrawScore.

authors.name: Haorui Chen
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Shiteng Lu

authors.institution: Institute of Agricultural Resources and Regional Planning
