papers.title: Some Results on the Complex Oscillation of Second-Order Linear Differential Equations
papers.abstract: We study the zeros of solutions of $f''+A(z)f=0$ with an entire coefficient $A$. We answer two questions of Gundersen affirmatively. We prove that if $A$ has finite order and the exponent of convergence of its distinct zeros is smaller than its order, then the zeros of the product of any two linearly independent solutions have infinite exponent of convergence. We also prove that if $A$ has finite order and the exponent of convergence of its zeros, counted with multiplicity, is smaller than its order, then the zeros of every non-trivial solution have infinite exponent of convergence.

authors.name: Shi-Jian Wu
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Finite-time stochastic resetting in bounded domains: competing targets, energetic cost, and optimal search strategies
papers.abstract: We investigate the first-passage dynamics and energetic cost of a Brownian particle subject to finite-time stochastic resetting in a bounded one-dimensional domain with two absorbing boundaries. Unlike conventional instantaneous resetting, the particle is returned to a prescribed resetting position through a finite-duration process driven by a linear trapping potential. By solving the corresponding backward equations, we derive analytical expressions for the mean global first-passage time and the splitting probabilities. Our results show that the finite duration of the return process can substantially modify the dependence of the mean global first-passage time on the resetting rate. In particular, we identify a critical trapping strength above which resetting can accelerate the search process, and characterize how the range of favorable resetting positions depends on the trapping strength. We further characterize the energetic cost of resetting by deriving the generating function of the total work and obtaining an analytical expression for its mean value. For the linear trapping potential considered here, we establish an exact relation between the mean total work and the mean cumulative return time. This relation allows us to establish a quantitative trade-off between the mean global first-passage time and the energetic expenditure, revealing how the finite duration of the return process affects search efficiency. Brownian dynamics simulations confirm our theoretical predictions.

papers.title: Weighing the Envelope: Component Weight and Arbitration in Envelope-Layer Defenses for a Single LLM Agent
papers.abstract: The envelope layer is the channel through which malicious content enters an LLM agent. Prior work established label and memory effects on multi-agent A2A envelopes, but the weight structure when MCP tools and memory coexist in a single agent remains unclear. Our threat model assumes an attacker pre-plants a malicious tool and poisons long-term memory; a benign user request inadvertently triggers it, and the attacker never enters the conversation. Following GDA Measurement and A/B/C/D, we measure how labels, memory, tool roles, and the backend shape invocation decisions across label-memory conflict, tool roles, robustness, and tool generalization. A tool-side forced-verification label substantially reduces semantic breach, but strong success memory pulls it back; a memory-side downgrade statement returns the outcome to the level of the label alone. The label works through mandatory implementation inspection plus default denial, not length or format; memory authorization wording erodes it with dose, while position and multi-turn pressure do not change the defense direction. Tool roles divide label effects into substitution, suppression, and boundary failure: low penetration is not safety, local leakage is the main residual risk, and a second malicious tool shows the same direction. Envelope labels are not a switch but a measurable, reversible weight constrained by backend and tool role, acting as a soft gate and risk signal within a broader defense rather than a substitute for permissions, sandboxing, or human review.

papers.title: Boundary $ C^{2, \gamma} $ regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s MTW condition
papers.abstract: We establish boundary regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s Ma--Trudinger--Wang condition. Let the source and target be bounded, mutually $ c $-convex domains in $ \mathbb{R}^n $, $ n\geqslant2 $, with $ C^{1,\beta} $ boundaries, and suppose that the cost is smooth, bi-twisted, and nondegenerate. For positive $ C^{0,\alpha} $ densities bounded away from zero and having equal total mass, we prove that both Kantorovich potentials belong to $ C^{2,\gamma} $ up to the boundary, where $ \gamma = \min\{\alpha,\beta\} $. Consequently, the optimal transport map is $ C^{1,\gamma} $ up to the boundary. The proof extends the monotonicity formula method of Collins and Tong to general costs through the geometry of the Kim--McCann metric. The resulting formula yields homogeneity of blow-up limits and uniform estimates for sections. These estimates give boundary obliqueness and allow comparison with solutions of the constant-density Monge--Amp\`ere equation, leading to the claimed regularity.

authors.name: Feng Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients
papers.abstract: We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. B\'erczi and Feh\'er conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient. We prove that generalized Bernoulli polynomials of real order at least their degree have simple real zeros. Applied to the shifted quotient, this gives strict ultra-log-concavity in the Schur index at every positive shift. For the original Newton coefficients, we establish strict log-concavity with an explicit multiplicative margin in two uniform regions. A Hahn projection gives a square-root band about the balanced Schur index; a complex saddle estimate extends this to a band of linear width. Uniform estimates for the cumulants of a normalized Schur functional give a terminal Newton region of linear width. Polynomial coefficient identities also establish every row with Schur index at most six or imbalance at most nine. The argument separates log-concavity in the Schur, derivative and Newton indices and identifies the factorial factors in the transfer between the latter two. The unrestricted Newton log-concavity conjecture remains open.

papers.title: Balanced Simplicial Complexes for the $\gamma$-Vectors of Zig-Zag Eulerian Polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a simplicial complex whose $f$-vector equals the $\gamma$-vector of the descent polynomial of an arbitrary canonically labeled rank-one poset. As an application, we prove Petersen and Zhuang's conjecture that the $\gamma$-vector of the normalized zig-zag Eulerian polynomial is the $f$-vector of a balanced simplicial complex.

authors.name: Lijie Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Once Upon a Bias: Gender Stereotyping in LLM-Generated Children's Stories
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to create stories for children. Since bedtime stories can shape children's perceptions of social roles, this raises concerns about whether LLMs adapt narrative portrayals according to the intended recipient's gender. We conducted a large-scale study to examine gender stereotyping in LLM-generated bedtime stories. Using matched daughter/son prompts and a five-generation design, we analyze 62,873 retained stories from 16 LLMs across 35 country settings and 12 narrator roles. We introduce a multi-level evaluation framework combining context-adjusted lexical rate contrasts, relative stereotype alignment, narrator-recipient interaction analysis, human evaluation, and representation-level interventions to examine both the consistency and interpretability of these differences. Our results reveal systematic differences in narrative framing: son-directed stories emphasize higher agency and lower communion compared to daughter-directed stories. While narrator gender expresses limited moderation on these patterns, high sociability exhibits a more pronounced interaction. Human evaluations demonstrate consistent agreement, although correspondence with lexical measures varies across narrative dimensions. Additionally, hidden-state analyses reveal decodable recipient-gender information. These findings demonstrate persistent yet context-dependent representational disparities in LLM-generated children's stories and motivate narrative-specific bias evaluation beyond short-form benchmarks.

papers.title: Incidence methods for algebraic expanders over arbitrary fields
papers.abstract:
Let $A\subset F$ be finite, $N=|A|$, $p=\operatorname{char}F$ (with $p=\infty$ in characteristic zero), and $L=1+\log(2N)$. In the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, we establish \[
  |AA+A|\gg N^{129/85}L^{-72/85}. \] This improves the long-standing $3/2$-exponent bound for $AA+A$ in positive characteristic in the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, without any assumption on the multiplicative doubling of $A$. We further establish uniform expansion bounds with exponents $129/85$ and $32/21$ for four families of three-variable product--quotient expanders, together with refined estimates over prime fields. For $\lambda\in F^\times$ and $N\le p^{1/2}$, our four-variable bounds include \[
  |AA+\lambda AA|\gg N^{214/135}L^{-7/9},\qquad
  |AA-AA|\gg_\varepsilon N^{6681/4175-\varepsilon}
  \quad(\varepsilon>0). \] In particular, several three- and four-variable targets admit uniform lower bounds with exponents greater than $3/2$ in the large-characteristic range. We also prove bounds with exponent $49/38$ for shifted products and shifted quotients, and for quadratic-image sumsets when $\operatorname{char}F\ne 2$, as well as characteristic-sensitive estimates for $AA+\lambda A/A$ and $(A-A)^\times/(A-A)^\times$. The proofs combine higher-energy inequalities, regularisation, and point--line incidences.

authors.name: Yao Zhi
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Experimental Hematology

papers.title: On p-adic asymptotic formulas for slope factors of L-functions of toric exponential sums
papers.abstract: Adolphson and Sperber expressed the unique unit root of the $L$-function of a toric exponential sum in terms of $A$-hypergeometric functions, whereas reciprocal zeros and poles of positive slope remain much less understood.We study complete rational factors of arbitrary prescribed slope in families satisfying a chain-level ordinary condition. Our main tool is a new contraction map arising from a twisted block LU factorization of the Frobenius matrix of a nuclear $\sigma$-module. Its fixed point produces an upper triangularization and the associated slope filtration, while explicit Schur-complement quotients of finite Frobenius iterates approximate the diagonal slope blocks with geometrically decreasing error. At a periodic fiber, successive cancellation in an ordered product of these approximations yields a quotient formed from two finite Frobenius iterates, and the characteristic polynomial of this quotient converges to the complete slope polynomial. Combined with the relative Dwork trace formula, this yields uniform $p$-adic asymptotic formulas for the complete slope factors of the $L$-functions of toric exponential sums. When the relevant slope blocks have rank one, the Schur complements reduce to ratios of leading principal minors and give asymptotic formulas for the individual reciprocal zeros and poles after cancellation.

papers.title: Chromatic heights of homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology of connective spectra
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum of height $m$. The chromatic redshift theorem implies that its $n$-fold iterated algebraic $K$-theory $K^{(n)}(R)$ has height $m+n$. Moreover, there is a natural map $K^{(n)}(R)\to (T^n\otimes R)^{hT^n}$, where $T^n\otimes R$ denotes the $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology. Hence it is natural to ask whether the target also has height $m+n$. Although this fails in general, we prove that it holds whenever $R$ is connective and $m\geq1$. Our proof is based on an iterative calculation using Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology. As an application, we determine the support of the $T^n$-homotopy fixed points of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ for $n=2,3$ with $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ equipped with any $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-form.

papers.title: Counting shorter even cycles in graphs forbidding an even cycle
papers.abstract: For graphs $H$ and $F$, the generalized Tur\'an number $\operatorname{ex}(n,H,F)$ is the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph. Let $C_m$ be a cycle on $m$ vertices. Liu and Wu (2026) proved that, for fixed integers $k>\ell\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2\ell},C_{2k})=\left(\frac{(k-1)_\ell}{2\ell}+o(1)\right)n^\ell$, where $(k-1)_\ell=(k-1)\cdots(k-\ell)$. In this paper, we determine the exact value of $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2\ell},C_{2k})$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and characterize the unique extremal graph.

papers.title: Residual Allan Stability under Periodic Auxiliary Ramsey Sampling
papers.abstract: The timing of auxiliary Ramsey measurements can change the frequency stability associated with a drifting pulse shift at a fixed nominal Fisher-information rate for a constant shift. For periodic instantaneous observations of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck shift with causal prediction between updates, we derive the exact residual covariance averaged over the update cycle and the corresponding Allan variance at arbitrary averaging times. Relative to a continuous Kalman reference at the same information rate, periodic estimation increases the cycle-averaged estimation-error variance, reduces the short-time residual Allan variance, and increases its long-time value. Its covariance decays more slowly at the origin and has a larger integral. We extend the result to instantaneous sensing of the sum of finitely many independent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck modes. Integrated observations preserve the short-time ordering for the scalar shift, and numerical calculations resolve the dependence of the crossover on window duration. A zero-order-hold comparison shows that the short-time ordering can change when the same estimator drives a different correction command. A three-level Ramsey model of coherent population trapping (CPT) maps the discriminator response to an effective information budget and illustrates how the dark times affect the choice of schedule.

papers.title: Idempotency Is Not Recovery: A Fault-Injection Study of Language-Model Agent Tool Actions
papers.abstract: When a language-model agent's tool call is interrupted, the action may already have changed an external system without confirmation. Retrying risks duplication; assuming success may conceal an action that never occurred. We study these failure modes in a controlled agent runtime combining authorization, an action ledger, target-side idempotency, reconciliation, and evidence sealing. We inject ten single-host fault classes and compare four configurations and three ablations using a target-side oracle separate from the runtime ledger. On each of Windows and Linux, 7,513 trials used 96 captured model responses from 24 constructed cases. In 200 known original crash and replay pairs, the full configuration recorded 0/200 repeated effects versus 117/200 for each simpler baseline. A ledger-related ablation had 170/170 orphaned effects versus 0/170 and 200/300 recovery successes versus 300/300 for the full configuration. Disabling reconciliation left 100/100 known post-effect crash outcomes ambiguous despite no observed duplicates. A separate supplement designed after the initial results and reusing the same inputs found a similar pattern under response loss or delay. The full runtime had about one-seventh of fail-open throughput, while injected evidence-write faults left 75/100 trials per platform unresolved. These findings distinguish duplicate suppression from recovery and identify their measured reliability and performance tradeoffs within the tested benchmark.

papers.title: Gopakumar-Vafa invariants and Mordell-Weil lattices
papers.abstract: Let $X\to B$ be a Weierstrass fibration with integral fibers from a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold to a del Pezzo surface. For a smooth curve $D\subset B$ with smooth inverse image $Y$, we decompose the moduli fiber of stable sheaves with Euler characteristic one and projected cycle $D$. In fiber degree $k$, its components are indexed by all sections $C$ of $Y\to D$ with $\tfrac12\langle C,C\rangle\leq k$, where $\langle\, ,\,\rangle$ is the Mordell--Weil height pairing. For infinitesimally rigid sections we compute the GV contributions, recovering the $E_8$ theta product over a $(-1)$-curve. We formulate the corresponding conjecture for families of sections.

authors.name: Lutian Zhao
authors.institution: China Automotive Technology and Research Center

papers.title: Efficient interlayer interactions in non-planar molecule/transition-metal dichalcogenide two-dimensional heterostructure
papers.abstract: Integration of molecules and two-dimensional (2D) atomic materials offer new opportunities for hybrid electronic devices. Most progress has focused on interfacing planar molecule. In contrast, incorporating non-planar molecules into 2D heterostructures remains challenging due to the three-dimensional orientations of ligands. Here we investigate interlayer interactions between discrete non-planar spin-crossover (SCO) molecules, [Fe(tBu2qsal)2] (FTBQS), monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spacers through optical spectroscopies. FTBQS features bulk molecular crystal layers and can be mechanically exfoliated, enabling deterministic assembly of clean hybrid heterostructures. Robust photoluminescence (PL) quenching, even with an hBN spacer, indicates efficient F\"orster resonance energy transfer with a long decay distance. Gate-dependent optical spectroscopy further identifies charge transfer from the doping shifts in the TMD layers due to the TMD/FTBQS electronic band alignment. Our results establish efficient interlayer interactions between non-plana, discrete molecules and 2D crystals for hybrid electrical, optical, and spintronic devices.

papers.title: A Weinstein manifold without any spherical Fukaya category
papers.abstract: We show that, after attaching a subcritical handle to $T^*\bP^2$ to obtain a manifold $M$, the integral wrapped Floer endomorphism algebra of a cotangent fibre admits no spherical refinement for any choice of brane structure; this obstructs the existence of any wrapped Fukaya category for $M$ over the sphere spectrum. We further discuss some features of the resulting Weinstein eight-manifold $M$, which is homotopy equivalent to $S^4$.

papers.title: Can AI Understand Indonesian Children's Book Illustrations? Compliance, Safety, and the Cultural Alignment Gap
papers.abstract: Children's book illustrations carry developmental, pedagogical, and cultural responsibilities that are often formally codified in guidelines. As AI systems begin entering children's publishing pipelines, both as evaluators and as generators, a natural question arises: can they reliably meet the structural, safety, and cultural standards required? We investigate this across three criteria: guideline compliance, safety, and cultural alignment, using Indonesia's Book Leveling Guideline as a government-issued evaluation framework with explicit visual criteria for four reading levels. To understand how well VLMs can identify and apply these guideline criteria, we first evaluate them on real published children's book pages and compare their assessments against a human baseline. To then examine whether AI-generated illustrations meet the same standards, we apply the VLM judge to images produced by two generation models and cross-check them against a subset of human illustrator raters. We find that VLMs are reliable on explicit criteria such as compliance and safety, but fall short on cultural alignment, systematically missing content that human raters flag as culturally inappropriate. AI-generated illustrations show the same blind spot: they satisfy structural and safety criteria but fail to capture implicit cultural details that human raters consistently identify.

papers.title: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization
papers.abstract: Autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models predict discrete action tokens with the next-token objective of their vision-language backbone, so the action tokenizer defines the interface between the policy and the robot. In bimanual manipulation, the two arms share a repertoire of movements yet coordinate through complementary roles, and an action representation should capture both. However, most existing tokenizers encode both arms as a single concatenated action vector, in which motion patterns common to the two arms are not shared and cross-arm dependencies remain entangled within each token. The policy must therefore learn both aspects implicitly. We propose Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization (BiCAT), which shares one motion representation across arms while conditioning each arm's tokens on its partner through symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder. The policy then predicts all tokens of each arm in parallel, generating the left arm first and the right arm conditioned on it. Across ten RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and six real-world tasks on three embodiments, BiCAT achieves the highest success among the compared tokenizers. In simulation, it improves mean success by 17.6 percentage points over the strongest of eight baselines, with the largest gains on tasks that require close coordination between the arms, while requiring only 40.5 ms per action chunk. These results suggest that the action tokenizer is a natural place to model bimanual coordination.

authors.name: Xuanwei Liu
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Zhongyi Luo
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Reliability is a user-specific property of large language models
papers.abstract: Public benchmarks support comparisons of large language model (LLM) capabilities, yet users can experience the same highly ranked model differently. Drawing on traditional software reliability, we argue that the reliability of an LLM service should be assessed for specified users and conditions of use. This requires more than a capability score: evaluation evidence must support a claim about failure during future operation. We distinguish testing to discover faults from testing to assess reliability and identify ten modelling considerations behind such claims. We propose a six-workstream research roadmap linking claim specification, dynamic operational profiles, graded outcomes and noisy judgements, local probabilistic robustness, interaction dependence, and statistical inference with reassessment. Local probabilistic robustness addresses the behavioural variation hidden when different concrete inputs are treated as the same task. Published findings and an illustrative customer-support example motivate the roadmap; its integrated validation remains an open research task. Reliability claims complement, but do not replace, separate safety and security arguments. Capability scores should therefore be complemented by versioned operational claims that state whose requirements are covered, under which conditions, and with what uncertainty.

authors.name: Xingyu Zhao
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Tight Broad-line Width-Luminosity Relation in Little Red Dots and Its Consequence for Virial Black Hole Masses
papers.abstract: JWST has uncovered compact high-redshift sources with red, $\sim 5000$ K optical continua and broad Balmer lines, known as "little red dots" (LRDs). Whether these lines trace gas orbiting a massive black hole or electron scattering in a dense, Eddington-limited envelope around a lighter black hole leaves inferred masses spanning $10^{4}$--$10^{8}\,M_\odot$. We test both pictures by uniformly refitting public JWST/NIRSpec spectra of 29 LRDs, 15 other JWST broad-line sources, and luminosity-matched SDSS quasars. At fixed $\mathrm{H}\alpha$ luminosity, LRD broad $\mathrm{H}\alpha$ widths are remarkably uniform: their intrinsic scatter is 0.054 dex ($<0.075$ dex at 95%), less than half that of quasars (0.12 dex), clustering near $1760\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ outside the three brightest sources. Because single-epoch virial masses scale as width squared, they scatter intrinsically by $<0.16$ dex at fixed $\mathrm{H}\alpha$ luminosity, making virial masses and mass functions nearly deterministic restatements of luminosity regardless of the underlying physics. Compared with the Keplerian speed $v_{\rm K}$ at the photosphere of an Eddington-limited envelope, computed from each source's measured continuum luminosity and temperature, observed widths are $2.5$--$3.0\,v_{\rm K}$ ($2\text{--}3\times$ standard expectations for virial factors $f_{\rm vir}\approx0.5\text{--}1$), with a quarter of the flux above escape speed and no detected continuum-luminosity dependence at fixed $\mathrm{H}\alpha$ luminosity. Bound orbits outside a spherical photosphere thus require sub-Eddington luminosities ($\leq 0.10\text{--}0.30\,L_{\rm Edd}$), whereas an Eddington or super-Eddington envelope requires uniform $2\text{--}3\times$ non-gravitational broadening within the $\mathrm{H}\alpha$-emitting gas.

authors.name: Haoyu Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: When Shuffling Fails: Token Recovery from Obfuscated KV Caches
papers.abstract:
LLM serving systems store, offload, and share KV caches, exposing token-level representations to infrastructure operators and co-tenants. Shuffled obfuscation combines secret linear transforms with fresh permutations, claiming security from b! possible shufflings. We show that input symmetry invalidates this counting argument: security depends on distinguishable outputs under chosen inputs. Repeated tokens produce identical first-layer Value rows, making every row permutation leave the data unchanged. Only auxiliary structures such as a single-row recovery marker vary, reducing the effective state space from b! to b.
  We construct Repeat-to-Reveal. The attacker collects the b distinguishable states from its own probes and exploits their rank-one differences to recover an equivalent denoiser without knowing the defender's secret parameters. A one-time calibration transfers across requests sharing the same secret epoch, enabling passive token-multiset recovery from subsequently observed cache blocks through public-model dictionary matching. We instantiate the attack on official KV-Cloak and evaluate 3,000 real WildChat user prompts across nine models and eleven configurations. The attack recovers the secret parameters with high accuracy and achieves 100 percent token-multiset recovery on GPU. Refreshing row-level secrets between epochs interrupts cross-request transfer, confirming secret reuse scope as the operative vulnerability. We further confirm orbit collapse on two other open-source defenses: the sequence-permutation implementation of Thomas et al. and PermLLM. The KV-Cloak developers invited a detailed report through their private vulnerability reporting channel.

authors.name: Haoyu Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
papers.abstract: Language models can gain capacity at little computational cost from n-gram embedding tables: large tables of learned vectors for short sequences of consecutive tokens, which are looked up and added to the model's input or to its intermediate layers. Recent designs commonly use a separate n-gram embedding table for each layer, which makes the tables costly in memory and prevents layers from sharing what they learn. Sharing a single table, however, gives every layer the same embedding and leaves no room for layer-wise preferences, and it performs poorly in practice. We propose Chorus, in which one set of n-gram embedding tables serves the whole network and every layer reads it in its own way. Each layer maps the refined embedding through its own projection layer, after rescaling its components by factors computed from its current hidden state. Chorus matches the quality of existing n-gram methods with 87% smaller tables: with 1.2B table parameters it predicts text better than FactorEngram and DeepSeek's Engram do with 9.6B. It outperforms Engram, TN-gram and FactorEngram in every setting where we compared them, across table sizes from 20M to 9.6B parameters. We also show that the recently proposed memory-efficient optimizer Ember works well with Chorus, saving 99.2% of table-optimizer memory compared with AdamW without degrading training performance. These results enable further scaling of n-gram embedding tables along the table-size axis by reducing memory use and allowing shared knowledge to be reused across layers.

authors.name: Stephen Chung
authors.institution: The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

papers.title: Optimal Stability for Bivariate Weighted Fourth-Order Inequalities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove sharp stability estimates for a two-component radial weighted fourth-order Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality in the two radial regimes for which the scalar optimizers are explicitly known and the corresponding spectral non-degeneracy holds. These regimes are \(4-N<\alpha<2,\ \ell=-\alpha\), and \(2<\alpha<N,\ \ell=4(\alpha-2)(N-2)/(N-\alpha)-\alpha\). Let $N\ge 3$, $p=2(N+\ell)/(N-4+\alpha)>2$, \(\mu_1,\mu_2\geq0\), \(\kappa>0\), and $r,s>1$ satisfy $r+s=p$. For radial pairs $(u,v)\in X_{\mathrm{rad}}\times X_{\mathrm{rad}}$, we determine the sharp constant $S_{r,s,\mu_1,\mu_2,\kappa}$ in the coupled inequality \[ S_{r,s,\mu_1,\mu_2,\kappa} \left(\int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^\ell\big(\mu_1|u|^p+\mu_2|v|^p+p\kappa |u|^r|v|^s\big)dx\right)^{2/p} \le \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^\alpha\big(|\Delta u|^2+|\Delta v|^2\big)dx . \] The sharp constant is expressed through the scalar sharp constant and the minimum of an explicit one-dimensional ratio function. We also characterize all extremals and prove sharp quantitative stability estimates. The stability exponent is determined by the degeneracy of the ratio minimizers: it is quadratic in the non-degenerate case and becomes square-root type in the degenerate case.

papers.title: DetailScale-SR: Decoupling Restoration and Continuous Detail Control for Real-World Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Real-world image super-resolution often seeks the most detailed plausible reconstruction, although more detail is not always desirable. The same degraded image may require restrained restoration, faithful reconstruction, or enhanced visual detail according to user intent. We present DetailScale-SR, a preference-conditioned framework that continuously controls reconstructed detail for a fixed low-resolution input without altering the scene being restored. Rather than relying on post-processing or repeatedly rewriting prompts, it learns a continuous family of reconstructions while separating content recovery from detail preference. This enables a smooth transition from conservative restoration to richly textured results under consistent input and semantic constraints. Its controllable range also extends beyond conventional restoration: DetailScale-SR can enhance high-frequency structures and generate perceptually richer textures than the paired high-resolution reference. Text restoration is another distinct strength. For text-rich scenes, especially Chinese posters and signs, it recovers more legible and character-faithful text than prior generative SR methods under matched textual guidance. DetailScale-SR therefore unifies continuous detail control, beyond-reference enhancement, and reliable recovery of semantically important content. Our model is available at https://modelscope.cn/models/DiffSynth-Studio/Qwen-Image-2.1-SR

authors.name: Jingjing Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: A combinatorial proof of a symmetric joint distribution on strict binary trees
papers.abstract: Nonplanar strict binary trees on $2n+1$ vertices are enumerated by the reduced tangent numbers $T_{2n+1}/2^n$, whose entries are refined by Poupard's triangle. Poupard defined the end of the minimal chain ($\mathrm{eoc}$) and the parent of the maximum leaf ($\mathrm{pom}$) on these trees, proving that $\mathrm{eoc}$ and $\mathrm{pom}+1$ share this triangular distribution. Foata and Han subsequently showed via tree calculus and partial difference equations that the joint distribution of $(\mathrm{eoc}, 2n+1-\mathrm{pom})$ is symmetric. By introducing an auxiliary tree statistic dual to $\mathrm{eoc}$, we give a bijective proof of this symmetry. Our proof composes a recursive bijection on strict binary trees, a bijection to alternating Andr\'e permutations, and the reverse-complement involution on permutations.

papers.title: Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients for Stable Feature Attribution
papers.abstract: Path-based attribution methods like Integrated Gradients (IG) are widely used to interpret neural networks, yet imperceptible input perturbations can drastically alter their attribution maps while leaving model predictions unchanged. We introduce Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients (ERIG), a path-based attribution method that intrinsically attenuates gradient irregularities along the integration path using maximum-entropy softmax weighting with temperature parameter $\tau$. We quantify the effect of the entropy-regularized weighting on attribution stability by using the Lipschitz properties of the model and its gradients. We decompose the attribution change under an input perturbation into a model-response term, whose bound is $\tau$-independent, and a weight-variation term, whose bound decreases at rate $\mathcal{O}(1/(2\tau))$. Their ratio $R(\tau)$ characterizes the trade-off between gradient information and attribution stability. We further add a new dimension to attribution evaluation by adapting classical noise estimators into two metrics, LINV-C and LINV-P, that quantify attribution noise. Across eleven CNN and Transformer backbones on ImageNet and Oxford-IIIT Pet datasets, our experiments show that, relative to the next-best method, ERIG remains comparable on ranking-based fidelity metrics while improving localization by approximately 24% and attribution stability by approximately 47-fold on average, reaching up to four orders of magnitude improvement over IG, all at negligible additional computational cost.

papers.title: Character codegrees in $\pi$-separable groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the set $\operatorname{C}_{\pi}(G)$ of irreducible characters of a finite $\pi$-separable group $G$ whose codegrees (defined by Qian as $\operatorname{cod}(\chi)=|G:\ker\chi|/\chi(1)$) are $\pi$-numbers, in relation to the Isaacs--Gajendragadkar classes of $\pi$-special characters $\operatorname{X}_{\pi}(G)$ and $\operatorname{B}_{\pi}$-characters $\operatorname{B}_{\pi}(G)$.

papers.title: Adaptive Line Switching for Cascade Mitigation in Power Systems via Graph Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Although cascading failures are relatively rare events in power systems, they pose significant risks and can lead to severe economic and societal consequences within a short period. Therefore, developing effective mitigation strategies to prevent cascade propagation and to minimize their impacts is essential. This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based framework for adaptive transmission line switching to mitigate cascading failures. Given the important role of network topology and component interactions in cascading failure propagation in power systems, graph-based DRL approaches, including Graph-DQN, Graph-A2C, and Graph-PPO frameworks, are developed to capture and utilize the topological information of power systems. The proposed frameworks are evaluated on the IEEE 39, 57, and 118 bus systems and benchmarked against the unmitigated case, random and heuristic-based switching strategies as baselines, as well as their corresponding graph-agnostic DRL counterparts. The results demonstrate the importance of incorporating graph information into these mitigation frameworks, leading to reduced cascade size, load loss, and network clustering.

papers.title: DORMS: Image Segmentation via Depth-Ordered Region Merge Trees
papers.abstract: We introduce DORMS (Depth-Ordered Region Merging for Segmentation), a purely algorithmic approach to image segmentation from monocular depth maps, requiring no neural networks or learned parameters in the segmentation process. An off-the-shelf monocular depth estimator provides the input depth maps. Our method constructs depth-ordered merge trees through a deterministic union-find sweep, combining component area, depth persistence, and spatial contact constraints to guide region merging. A threshold search determines the segmentation granularity according to a specified target region count, while global depth detrending improves the separation of local geometric structures. Extensive experiments on COCO Panoptic, Cityscapes, and ADE20K demonstrate consistent improvements over classical segmentation baselines and competitive performance against zero-shot neural segmentation models. Notably, our method outperforms all evaluated zero-shot models on Cityscapes, while remaining competitive with several approaches on COCO and ADE20K. These results highlight the potential of purely algorithmic geometric reasoning for image segmentation without learned segmentation models.

papers.title: Language Models Make New Research Sound Old
papers.abstract: Researchers are increasingly using large language models (LLMs) to validate research questions. We find that LLMs make open research questions sound partly studied and overstate what related papers establish. Models recognize most of these overstatements when asked to check the papers' full texts separately. On 40 questions drawn from newly accepted papers, GPT-6-Astra correctly judges 98% to be unstudied, but states that status plainly in only 8% of ordinary answers. All six frontier systems show reporting gaps of 30-90 percentage points. Across 22 models given identical papers, higher capability is associated with more accurate judgments and larger reporting gaps. This reporting failure is asymmetric: models correctly identify studied questions in 88-100% of ordinary answers when we supply the answering papers. To correct this, we build a fixed answer from each model's judgment and separate checks of cited papers. This raises Astra's clear reporting of open status from 8% to 95%, with improvements in all six systems. Finally, we predict reviewers' novelty grades by combining several models' written ratings with a rule learned from graded examples, reaching the performance range reported by Think-Probe-Respond. Unlike TPR, our approach needs no access to model weights or internal activations, so it also works with closed-weight frontier models.

papers.title: Linear Connectivity of Boundaries of Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
papers.abstract:
To every right-angled Coxeter group one can canonically associate a hyperbolic metric space, called its maximized hyperbolic space. This space is Morse recognizing and is obtained from the Davis complex by coning off its standard product regions. We characterize, purely in terms of the defining graph, when the Gromov boundary of a maximized hyperbolic space is nonempty and linearly connected.
  As an application, we prove that among one-ended right-angled Coxeter groups, splitting over a subgroup of an unbounded product subgroup is a quasi-isometry invariant. We also establish several features shared by maximized hyperbolic spaces and curve graphs, including the existence of dead ends and visibility of boundaries. Moreover, when the boundary is nonempty, it is non-compact if and only if the defining graph contains an induced 4-cycle.

papers.title: On the self-extensions of the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence over $\mathbb{Q}_p$
papers.abstract: Let $p\ge5$ and $D$ be the unique nonsplit quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We compute, in the category of smooth representations with a fixed central character, the self-extension groups of the $D^{\times}$-representations occurring in the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence in the generic case. The main ingredient is a new weighted filtration on the relevant ring and module. The associated graded module preserves the first nontrivial extension relation, which is not detected by the $\mathfrak{m}_D$-adic filtration.

authors.name: Chenhao Tang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Finite-dimensional Hopf algebras generated by the coradical
papers.abstract:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over a field $k$. The paper is concerned with the question of when $H$ is generated by the coradical $H_0$. We give several characterizations of this property, involving the largest Hopf ideal contained in the Jacobson radical $J(H^*)$ and the coefficient coalgebra of the injective hull of the trivial comodule. If the canonical map $H_0\to H/J(H)$ is surjective, then $H$ is generated by $H_0$ if and only if $H=H_0^3+J(H)^2$, where $H_0^3$ is the span of products of three elements of $H_0$.
  For finite locally free Hopf algebras of constant rank over a $k$-scheme in characteristic zero, including duals of liftings of a given Nichols algebra, the locus where this property holds is Zariski open and compatible with arbitrary base change.
  For a finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $K$ with abelian coradical over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the largest Hopf ideal contained in $J(K)$ is determined. $K^*$ is generated by its coradical if and only if $J(K)$ contains no nonzero skew-primitive elements. For liftings of quantum linear spaces and standard liftings of finite Cartan type, this condition is expressed in terms of the deformation parameters of $K$.

papers.title: Emo-H2A: Driving a Facial Robot Directly from LLM Hidden States at Token Rate
papers.abstract: Diverse, semantically synchronized, and low-latency facial expressions are essential for human-robot interaction. While large language models (LLMs) have endowed anthropomorphic robots with fluent speech, facial expression still struggles to follow the conversation. Motivated by this gap, we present Emo-H2A (hidden-to-actuation), a paradigm that drives a facial robot directly from LLM hidden states during autoregressive decoding. Without a separate emotion label, expression stays continuous and context-sensitive, and the face moves with the unfolding reply. We instantiate this paradigm as EmoManifold, a training-free method that extracts a valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) coordinate from each hidden state, projects it, and drives the face at token granularity. The readout is checked on six language models, and the same projection drives our 29-degree-of-freedom (DoF) facial robot. When driven by this projection, the face shifts its expression in the matching direction on 87.5% of within-reply valence transitions, whereas holding a single label for the whole reply leaves directional tracking near the 50% chance level, and first moves in 0.96s rather than waiting 10-26s for the reply to finish and a turn-level label to return.

authors.name: Zhouping Yin
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Schatten and weak Schatten classes of composition operator differences on Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: We investigate Schatten and weak Schatten class membership of differences of composition operators on the standard weighted Bergman spaces over the unit disk. We prove that the known sufficient condition for Schatten p-class membership is also necessary for 0<p<2, thereby completing the characterization for all p>0. We also characterize when differences of composition operators belong to weak Schatten classes for every p>0. Both results are expressed in terms of local-mass conditions involving the pseudohyperbolic distance between the inducing maps, and yield two-sided (quasi-)norm estimates.

papers.title: Local connectivity of friends-and-strangers graphs with a star
papers.abstract: Given two finite simple graphs $X$ and $Y$ with the same number of vertices, the vertex set of the friends-and-strangers graph $\FS(X,Y)$ consists of all bijections from the vertices of $X$ to the vertices of $Y$. Two bijections are adjacent exactly when one is obtained from the other by swapping the images of two adjacent vertices of $X$, while leaving all other images unchanged, and the two swapped images are adjacent in $Y$. For $n\ge2$, let $\Star_n$ be the star on $n$ vertices. Krishnan and Li [Electron. J. Combin. 33 (2026), no. 3, Paper P3.41] conjectured that, for $n\ge3$, whenever $\FS(X,\Star_n)$ is connected, the maximum number of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths between any two distinct vertices is equal to the smaller of their degrees. We prove this conjecture. More precisely, if $\FS(X,\Star_n)$ is connected, then $X$ must be $2$-connected, and the conjectured equality holds for every pair of distinct vertices. We further prove the stronger result that, whenever $X$ is $2$-connected, the same equality holds in every connected component of $\FS(X,\Star_n)$.

papers.title: What Moves the Ceiling on Automated Audit: from General Code to Scientific Code, Results and Data
papers.abstract: Models increasingly check what other models write. We study one shipped arrangement, in which an auditor from a different vendor reads the work and deterministic checks verify what code can verify, and measure its limits against ground truth no model supplies. On general-purpose code with hidden tests, eight readings of the auditor reach 30.0% recall [20.0, 40.7] at 16.0% [10.1, 22.3] flags on correct code, with diminishing returns and no plateau. The reading model (confounded with its sampling), one rulebook sentence and the decision rule each move that figure, and much of what is missed is, on a post hoc rating, behaviour the specification never determined. In three preregistered science studies, checking that reported numbers trace to their sources flagged all 49 inconsistent reports and none of 25 consistent fabrications, of which the model auditor flagged 23 (21 with a sound finding, post hoc); on data, a documentation-derived validator and the auditor flagged overlapping but different faulty items, together 112 of 140 at a 2.9% [0.7, 5.7] flag rate on clean data; and on scientific code, reframing the task around one step cut flags on correct code from 68.7% to 36.0%. Where both tiers ran, the deterministic one flagged no clean item and could not see consistent error; the model saw some and erred itself. Studies making model calls were preregistered, the two unregistered analyses are named, and every quoted report passed independent cross-vendor review.

papers.title: Global nonsolvability of the leafwise $\dbar$-equation on foliations with Stein leaves
papers.abstract: Motivated by our previous work on $q$-convexity and global solvability for Levi flat structures, we study the complex foliation associated with the non-tame family of Stein structures constructed by Forstneri\v c and Sigur\dh ard\'ottir. Although every leaf is closed and biholomorphic to $\C^2$ and the foliation admits a complete bundle-like Riemannian metric, there exists a smooth leafwise $\dbar$-closed $(0,1)$-form for which the leafwise $\dbar$-equation admits no global $L^r_{\loc}$ solution for any $0<r\le\infty$. This result also suggests a modification of Questions~2.10.4--2.10.6 in \emph{Foliations: Dynamics, Geometry and Topology}.

authors.name: Jun Yao
authors.institution: China University of Petroleum, East China

papers.title: Sharp Partial Regularity of Weakly Pseudoholomorphic Maps Into Projective Algebraic Varieties
papers.abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we prove that a weakly pseudoholomorphic $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ map from a real-analytic almost complex $2m$-manifold into a projective algebraic variety has a countably $(2m-4)$-rectifiable singular set. When $m=2$, the singular set is shown to be locally finite. We first establish both conclusions on smooth almost complex domains under the additional assumption that the pullback of the Fubini--Study form is distributionally closed. We then show that this conservation law follows from the Cauchy--Riemann equation alone on real-analytic domains.

papers.title: AppSec Core: An Ontology for Security-by-Design Software Engineering
papers.abstract: When engineers or coding agents change an application, a dependency, a configuration or a build pipeline, they need to know three things: which security rules apply, how to meet them, and what evidence to leave. Today the answers are spread over many standards, frameworks, laws and lists of weaknesses, and each one uses its own words and level of detail. This paper presents AppSec Core, a model of the security work that engineers do. It says what must be true, which practices get there, which mechanisms do the job and which artefacts show that it was done. It has 259 elements in ten domains. We built it from a security-by-design manual written from practice, and then checked it against 31 outside sources, ten of them about AI systems and agents. Along the way we made three changes, which added five objectives and made one domain wider. We did not need a new domain. Most objectives are backed by several sources: the typical objective is used by six of the twenty technical sources, and 194 of the 202 objectives, practices and mechanisms are linked to items in the sources. For the domain of a change, the model gives back a closed set of typed elements, and for a source, it gives back the objectives that the source points to. We keep the model apart from the manual, the selection rules and the server that delivers the result, and we follow one change, adding a third-party package, through all four. When a code generator received the requirements, the share of security tests passed on a public benchmark went from 77.4% to 93.0%. On a second benchmark, the result was close to that of the benchmark's own "oracle" prompt, which is written with the tests in mind.

papers.title: Spatial Extremes on Domains with Physical Barriers
papers.abstract:
We propose a model for spatial extremes what realistically accommodates nonconvex domains. Most existing models assume that tail dependence between locations depends only on their separation. Even if extended to be anisotropic or nonstationary, they still cannot accommodate features between points that may mediate the dependence. This assumption limits their applicability in settings where physical barriers like mountains, coastlines, or islands may attenuate or even block dependence in extreme events.
  In this work, we use the idea of a visibility graph to modify an existing spatial random scale model. This results in a tail dependence model that naturally accommodates nonconvex spatial domains, where the nonconvex features are interpreted as physical barriers. Furthermore, the model inherits key properties from the scale mixture like the ability to represent asymptotic independence at long ranges and either asymptotic dependence or asymptotic independence at short ranges.
  We apply our model to two applications in which physical barriers feature prominently in determining the spatial structure of extreme events. The first is precipitation in the South Island of New Zealand, where the Southern Alps shelter the eastern region from the effects of atmospheric rivers which arrive from the west. The second is significant wave heights in the North Atlantic, where the Faroe Islands tend to block the effects of extratropical cyclones traveling into the North Sea.

papers.title: From Arraignment to Resolution: Transformer Models of Court Cases
papers.abstract: The criminal legal system is composed of many complex decision points, such as which charges are pursued, how bond is determined, plea deal negotiations, and sentencing. Given the profound impact of such decisions, there is a growing need to increase the transparency within this system. While prior machine learning approaches have focused on modeling single decisions (e.g., recidivism), this paper proposes a transformer-based time series model to forecast the outcome of the next proceeding in a case (e.g., charges accepted, bond set, plea deal made, etc.). By modeling a case as an event sequence, we enable a more nuanced analysis to support better oversight and understanding of decision making. We conduct an empirical analysis of thousands of cases using a newly constructed dataset derived from publicly available court records of a mid-sized U.S. city. We fit models that combine textual data from clerk notes with structured information about the defendant, prior charges, and courtroom. Our transformer model achieves $.57$ micro-F1 on a 20-class multi-label task, a significant improvement over several baselines and comparable to a GRU trained on the same input. We demonstrate how the model can be used to provide insights into decision-making and help court observers identify emerging issues within the jurisdiction studied.

papers.title: From Docket Minutes to Case Trajectories: Building Analysis-Ready Criminal Court Data
papers.abstract: Criminal court records are often fragmented, noisy, and siloed, making it challenging for both legal experts and community stakeholders to access and analyze court data to identify trends and provide public oversight. In this paper, we introduce a system for data ingestion, harmonization, and dashboard visualization designed for New Orleans criminal court proceedings data, aimed at both expert and lay audiences. Our system collects and harmonizes disparate data, generates case trajectories, and provides intuitive visualization techniques based on community feedback to analyze demographics, temporal trends, and specific case events. We demonstrate the system through an exploratory analysis of recent short-term trends and policy impacts within New Orleans, illustrating how it can support the investigation of anomalies, policy changes, and procedural irregularities. We also present feedback from a small formative study of community stakeholders who have helped co-design and use the system, suggesting that it may improve access to and interpretation of local court data.

papers.title: Error Analysis of Deep Learning
papers.abstract: This review examines deep learning theory through the lens of error decomposition, systematically addressing approximation, statistical, and optimization errors. We trace the development of error analyses from bounds on individual error components to frameworks that account for all three. Using nonparametric regression and the Deep Ritz Method as dual running examples, we demonstrate how these analyses apply across fundamentally different loss structures. We then review representative analyses in scientific machine learning, generative learning, reinforcement learning, representation learning, and large language models, showing how learning errors affect solutions, distributions, and predictions through problem-specific arguments. Throughout, we clarify which error components are controlled, how they are combined, and what assumptions are needed to obtain guarantees for trained networks.

papers.title: An Explicit Uniform Connectivity Bound for Generalized Markoff Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $X_D$ be the surface $x^2+y^2+z^2-xyz=D$ over $\mathbb F_p$. For every prime $p>10^{320}$ and every $D\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{4\}$, we prove that the three Vieta involutions act transitively on the trace triples of generating pairs of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$. The proof combines an explicit primitive-fiber argument, Chen's orbit-size lower bound, and a weighted maximal-divisor estimate. We also give an explicit descent from Nielsen transitivity to transitivity under the Vieta involutions alone.

papers.title: Half-Line Hardy-Szeg\H{o} Point Processes: Fisher-Hartwig Asymptotics and Sparse Conditioning
papers.abstract: A horizontal window extending from a fixed positive height to infinity has infinite area but a finite expected number of Hardy-Szeg\H{o} zeros. We study its zero count as the horizontal length $L$ grows. Unlike for fixed bounded-height windows, the logarithmic moment generating function has a new $\theta^2\log L/(2\pi^2)$ term; we also identify its holomorphic order-one correction. The logarithmic term has two equal contributions: a Fisher-Hartwig jump in a canonical Wiener-Hopf model and an endpoint effect in the original Fourier-Laplace operator. This yields precise point and tail probabilities at positive count densities. We also determine the transition when a moving upper height is comparable to $L$. For sparse exact counts $n_L\to\infty$ with $n_L=o(L)$, we obtain logarithmic probability asymptotics relative to the exact void probability. We determine the void exponent and sharp asymptotics relative to the void probability for counts up to order $\log L$. Under sparse exact-count conditioning, the empirical distribution of rescaled horizontal positions and logarithmic heights converges to the uniform law on the unit square. Near distinct interior horizontal locations, the rescaled configurations converge to independent Poisson processes with uniform logarithmic-height marks.

authors.name: Xiang Fang
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Geometric Imprint of a Tilted Accretion Disk in Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Gravitational wave astronomy has opened a new window onto black holes and the dynamics of strong-field gravity, while accretion flows offer a complementary and natural laboratory for probing strong-field physics. In this work, we show that the gravitational wave emission from an initially tilted accretion disk carries a distinct imprint of its orientation. We perform three dimensional general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations and evaluate the gravitational waves through Teukolsky equation. For an aligned disk, the emission is concentrated in low-$|m|$ modes, where $m$ is the azimuthal quantum number. For the initially tilted disk, higher-$|m|$ modes make a larger relative contribution. As the tilted flow subsequently aligns with the black hole spin, the contribution of $|m|\ge2$ modes decreases, showing strong correlation with the tilt angle. This indicates that the gravitational waves generated by the black hole environment carries geometric information about the surrounding matter. Our results establish a route towards using multimode gravitational radiation to probe the geometry and dynamical evolution of accretion flows in the strong-field region.

authors.name: Chen Yuan
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Obsolescence of High-Level Code: Agentic Generation from Semantic Artifacts
papers.abstract:
This paper argues that high-level source code need not remain the primary persistent artifact of software development when AI agents can generate, validate, and regenerate executable implementations from semantic intent. We place this claim in historical context by revisiting application generators, CASE tools, model-driven development, and platforms such as GeneXus, where developers already maintained higher-level representations from which code and other artifacts were derived.
  We propose a unifying view in which generation is the fundamental operation: given a semantic specification S = (R, C, I, T, O), maintained as the semantic authority, an agent produces a generated executable artifact A. Functional requirements, contracts, and interfaces are assessed as semantic obligations, while tests and operational objectives are assessed by an explicit external oracle V(A, S). We operationalize this framework through an experiment in independent generation: multiple LLVM artifacts are generated directly from one frozen semantic authority and evaluated by the same external oracle.
  The experiment reports regeneration coherence on an evaluated domain, not a proof of absolute correctness. It provides initial evidence that independently generated executable artifacts can produce the same observable outcomes under a common semantic authority and external oracle. We conclude by discussing reproducibility, specification-centered evolution, and the implications of treating implementation representation as a deployment choice rather than the primary maintained artifact.

papers.title: ADSPICE: A Method of Automatic Differentiation for Gradient-Based Lumped Circuit Optimization with Native SPICE
papers.abstract: This work presents a novel computer-aided design (CAD) tool for gradient-based circuit optimization using SPICE and automatic differentiation, which we term ADSPICE. Automatic differentiation (AD) is a technique for evaluating a derivative by breaking it into its elementary differentiation operations and repeatedly applying the chain rule, in contrast with a finite-difference-based derivative computed from a small perturbation. Native SPICE (realized with ngspice) is equipped with automatic differentiation toward gradient-based optimization, particularly adjoint-mode optimization. This is implemented with custom C code and shared library control, allowing easy integration with existing SPICE infrastructure. We show a computational performance analysis, demonstrating faster optimization vs. an existing finite-difference method, SPICE OPUS, the closest competitor in SPICE optimization tools. The result is a speedup factor of 383x for the largest circuit compared within the state-of-the-art, SPICE OPUS. For circuit sizes above approximately 3,500 nodes, the time taken by ADSPICE optimization decreases with increasing problem size, as a proportion of total computational time. The speed bottleneck is shown to be SPICE solves rather than ADSPICE enhancements. Voltage gradients needed for forward-mode AD are benchmarked against Xyce, another state-of-the-art simulator, using an integrated CMOS operational amplifier test circuit. The results match with a maximum error of 0.203%, further validating the accuracy of our method. ADSPICE is shown to enable SPICE, and SPICE-based simulators, with automatic differentiation for gradient optimization, without requiring creation of a new circuit simulator.

papers.title: Supervised Hebbian Class Networks: Learning Without Backpropagation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Supervised Hebbian Class Networks as a method for training multi- layer perceptrons and convolutional networks without gradient calculations or backpropa- gation. Each neuron in a learned layer is assigned a class, while connections follow the usual fully connected or convolutional pattern. The method combines a class-based supervision rule shared across layers with a Lion optimizer adapted to Hebbian activity products. All layers train together throughout the run, and their activities provide class predictions di- rectly, without a separately trained classifier. The experiments test the method on MNIST with a multilayer perceptron and on CIFAR-10 with a convolutional networ

papers.title: Positron escape from dark matter spikes in black hole X-ray binaries
papers.abstract: Chan and Lee present a model where the AMS-02 positron excess is explained by dark matter (DM) annihilation in spike halos around nearby black holes A0620-00 and XTE J1118+480. Their model assumes a uniform magnetic and diffusive environment en route to Earth. Thus, it depends on the assumption that one can ignore the small-scale, near-horizon environment in the diffusion-loss equation. We demonstrate that this is not the case. An accurate magnetic field model near the horizon means, without increasing the required cross-section by a factor of roughly 500 to 1400, depending on the transport near the horizon, the positron flux from these sources cannot account for a significant fraction of the AMS-02 excess.

papers.title: Modeling and Stability of Power Systems With Coupled Data Center and Grid Dynamics
papers.abstract: The growing deployment of data centers poses challenges for power-system operation. However, data centers possess flexible resources that can be leveraged to mitigate their impact on the grid and provide grid services. This paper develops a linear-affine dynamic model of a transmission network with multiple data centers, explicitly coupling electromechanical grid dynamics with data center power demand and computational backlog. Grid-aware computing policies are incorporated to represent how data centers adjust their computational power in response to grid frequency deviations and workload backlog. The proposed framework provides a tractable means of investigating the interactions between multiple data centers and the transmission grid and assessing the potential of flexible computing to support power-system stability.

papers.title: A Geometric Calder\'on Problem for Differential Forms
papers.abstract: We establish boundary determination and global partial-data uniqueness for Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential $p$-forms. We derive an explicit recursion for its full symbol and determine the full boundary jet of the metric, modulo conformal gauge in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$. For $p\geq1$, partial data determine metrics that are analytic in the interior and near the measured boundary subset, up to isometry or conformal equivalence. The global uniqueness relies on a new projection-kernel embedding that detects the unobserved boundary through rank loss and small eigenvalues. We also establish global partial-data uniqueness for smooth metrics with harmonic curvature, using elliptic-transport unique continuation and, in the critical dimension, conformal-geodesic coordinates. A Weyl nondegeneracy condition further upgrades conformal equivalence to isometry.

authors.name: Zuoqin Wang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Optimized Flight Control for Interception of High-Altitude Maneuvering Targets
papers.abstract: We implement and compare two approaches to improving flight control system (FCS) performance using reinforcement meta-learning (meta-RL). Both approaches are evaluated in a terminal phase hypersonic intercept engagement requiring hit-to-kill accuracy against a highly agile maneuvering target. In the first approach (FCS-RL), meta-RL is used to optimize a full FCS that maps acceleration tracking error and other measurements directly to commanded channel deflection rates of change, combining pitch, yaw, and roll control into a single policy. In contrast, the second approach (FCS-3L-RL) starts with a standard FCS (FCS-3L) implementing a three-loop autopilot for pitch and yaw control, but adapts the scheduled autopilot gains in real time using a policy optimized with meta-RL. Both approaches are compared to the FCS-3L in a 6-DOF simulator that captures most factors relevant to guidance and flight control. Simulations show that under ideal conditions the three systems have comparable performance. However, under conditions of aerodynamic uncertainty, radome refraction, or target evasive maneuvers, the FCS-RL significantly outperforms the FCS-3L-RL with improved intercept probability and less control effort. In turn, the FCS-3L-RL outperforms the FCS-3L by a similar margin. Importantly, we demonstrate that both FCS-RL and FCS-3L-RL generalize well to novel engagement scenarios, flight conditions, and target maneuvers that are not experienced during the optimization process.

papers.title: RefinementGuard: Counterexample-Directed Semantic Qualification for Hidden Agent-Tool Execution
papers.abstract: Tool runtimes can lower an agent-selected operation into a hidden parallel graph, reducing latency and context while risking semantic mistranslation. We introduce RefinementGuard: translation validation for hidden, effectful agent-tool lowerings, coupled to artifact-bound, fail-closed runtime admission. Qualification compares a candidate graph with an independent reference on isolated state using explicit parent-operation obligations. We evaluate two repository-level contracts, bug localization and patch validation, on controlled repositories. Among 100 activated, non-equivalent development/qualification faults adjudicated by one human, parent-semantic validation rejects 49/100 (operator-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [33.7%, 64.8%]). The objective is selective admission, not maximum mutation rejection: exact equality rejects 100/100 faults but also all 60 valid variants, whereas obligation-based validation accepts 60/60; its 51 residual misses identify concrete specification gaps. On a frozen disjoint input split, the held-out B2-B3 result is localization-only because 21 patch mutants fail structurally; B3 rejects 38/56 localization defects. In a controlled asynchronous-delay regime, the localization serial/guarded median-latency ratio is 4.50x, and hidden execution exposes 74.3% less parent-visible context than visible execution. Patch validation shows no demonstrated speedup; zero-delay runs expose overhead. End-to-end qualification thus detects lower-layer misses while preserving localization's parallelism.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Crystal Structure Elucidation from Powder X-Ray Diffraction with Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Determining unique atomic coordinates from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) remains challenging because peak overlap, weak scattering from light elements, limited scattering contrast between elements with similar atomic numbers, and experimental noise render the inverse problem underdetermined. Here, we present XCAPE (XRD-Constrained Accelerated Prediction Engine), a crystal structure prediction (CSP) framework that integrates experimentally derived composition, unit cell parameters, space group, and PXRD data into a symmetry-aware evolutionary search. XCAPE explores Wyckoff-site configurations using tailored mutation operations, evaluates candidates by both energetic stability and diffraction agreement, and accelerates geometry optimization using a universal machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP). The framework recovered 71 of 77 database-derived benchmark structures (92.2%) from simulated PXRD patterns and all 12 reference structures from experimental PXRD patterns. It further identified 12 candidate structure assignments that are consistent with experimental PXRD patterns, lack matching entries in the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database (ICSD), and are thermodynamically competitive at the MLIP level. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations showed that 10 of these 12 candidates lie within 10 meV/atom of the convex hull. By bridging experimental diffraction data and physically plausible atomistic models, XCAPE can provide structural insight into previously unresolved materials and support accelerated materials discovery in automated research workflows.

papers.title: TapTacTouch: Shape Completion from Sparse Tactile Contacts with Geometric Priors
papers.abstract: 3D object reconstruction is essential for robotic perception and manipulation, yet conventional approaches predominantly rely on visual observations that can be limited by occlusion or unavailable in visually constrained environments. In this work, we propose a vision-free, training-free, and category-agnostic framework for reconstructing 3D object meshes from sparse tactile contacts without relying on pretrained shape models. A 6-DoF robotic arm equipped with a 20-DoF multi-finger robotic hand collects tactile observations using 3x3 pressure sensor arrays mounted on the finger pads. The acquired tactile measurements are transformed into 3D contact constraints through robot kinematics and integrated into a multi-scale Gaussian Process Implicit Surface (GPIS). To address sparse and incomplete surface observations, the proposed method incorporates contact confidence weighting, weak pseudo-surface constraints, and an observation-driven geometric prior to preserve local surface geometry and provide structural guidance in unobserved regions. Real-world experiments on six objects achieve a Chamfer Distance (CD) of 1.610, an Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) of 7.738, and an F-Score of 95.00, with reconstruction completed in an average of 49.99 s per object. These results demonstrate that sparse tactile sensing can provide sufficient geometric information for continuous 3D object reconstruction without visual or semantic information.

papers.title: CounselTraj: Synthesizing Process-Aware Psychological Counseling Dialogues via Dialogue-Act Trajectory Planning
papers.abstract: The growing demand for psychological counseling has motivated the development of LLM-based systems that support human counselors, but training such systems requires large-scale, high-quality dialogue data. Authentic counseling transcripts are difficult to collect and share because of privacy concerns, making synthetic dialogues an important alternative. However, existing synthetic datasets, despite covering diverse scenarios and client profiles, often consist of brief exchanges and fail to capture session-level counseling processes. We propose CounselTraj, a dialogue-act trajectory planning framework for expanding brief synthetic dialogues into process-aware, session-level psychological counseling dialogues. CounselTraj learns dialogue-act patterns from role-play counseling dialogues produced by human counselors, plans coordinated trajectories for clients and counselors, and uses them as flexible guidance for long-form dialogue generation. Experiments across three Chinese synthetic counseling datasets show that CounselTraj produces more complete and coherent sessions with higher-quality counselor interventions than both direct expansion and expansion with randomly sampled trajectories. Based on CounselTraj, we construct CounselTrajD, a dataset containing over 10K process-guided Chinese psychological counseling dialogues, and use it to train CounselTrajLM for counseling response generation. Evaluations at both the response and session levels show that CounselTrajLM outperforms publicly available Chinese counseling models in response quality, therapeutic understanding and intervention, and counseling-process coherence and progress. Our code and model are publicly available at https://github.com/UEC-InabaLab/CounselTraj.

papers.title: Evaluating invariance training with certified answer-changing controls in neural graph algorithms
papers.abstract: Invariance training aims to make neural algorithmic reasoners robust to answer-preserving input changes and is judged by accuracy and by how rarely such edits change predictions. We ask whether this evaluation detects lost sensitivity to answer-changing edits on minimum spanning trees of synthetic graphs, where both directions can be certified. Attaching a subgraph through one bridge provably preserves every original label. Attaching it through two edges, oracle-selected to change a label, and lowering one weight inside the graph serve as answer-changing controls; a response is a changed prediction on an edge whose label changes. A reproduced graph transformer (GDT) within its published accuracy range changes a provably fixed label on 53.3-65.9% of the 64-vertex graphs it solves exactly after a 64-vertex bridge attachment; removing the connecting edge changes little. With 16-vertex graphs and attachments, three invariance objectives lower GDT violations from 2.91% to 0.52-2.02% of pairs at essentially unchanged accuracy. Training also lowers the response to two-edge attachments from 97.6% to 66.0-79.0%, while the response to in-base weight edits stays near 99.5%. At 64 vertices accuracy also falls, but on 16-vertex bases only the attachment control reveals the loss. A message-passing network loses some attachment response at small penalty weights but gains little invariance. Running the conventionally trained GDT on each biconnected block separately removes all observed violations and keeps accuracy and both responses, so the task does not force the trade-off. Sensitivity checks for trained invariance should include certified answer-changing edits that attach material as the training edits do.

papers.title: On Jacquet Modules of Principal Series in Families
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a $p$-adic field $F$. Let $Y$ be the diagonalizable affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}[p^{-1},p^{1/2}]$ parametrizing weakly unramified characters of a minimal Levi $M$. The relative Weyl group $W$ acts on $Y$. We define a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{J}$, called the universal Jacquet module, on the fiber product $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$. The fibers of $\mathcal{J}$ can be identified with the duals of spaces of intertwining operators between weakly unramified principal series representations of $G$.
  We use the geometry of $Y\times_{Y/\!/W}Y$ to study the fundamental properties of $\mathcal{J}$. In particular, we determine the invertible locus of $\mathcal{J}$. Thus we show that for any field $k$ with $\operatorname{char}k\neq p, p^{1/2}\in k$ and any weakly unramified character $\chi\in Y(k)$, the normalized Jacquet module $\pi_{\chi,N}$ of the normalized parabolic induction $\pi_{\chi}=\operatorname{ind}_P^G\chi$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}(\chi\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ as an $\mathcal{O}(Y)$-module if and only if $\operatorname{End}_G(\pi_{\chi})\cong k$. This addresses the precise non-semisimple structure of Jacquet modules in the scalar endomorphism case. Specializing to the case in which $G$ is split, $\chi$ is trivial, and $k=\mathbb{C}$, this proves a conjecture of Dipendra Prasad. We also show that the isomorphism $\pi_{\chi,N}\cong\mathcal{O}(\chi\times_{Y/\!/W}Y)$ cannot be defined canonically over the family of characters $\chi$ satisfying $\operatorname{End}_G(\pi_{\chi})\cong\mathbb{C}$, by showing that the restriction of $\mathcal{J}$ to its invertible locus is a nontrivial line bundle if the relative root system of $G$ contains an irreducible component of rank at least two.

authors.name: Yuheng Hao
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: MoMoVL: Modality-Aware Adaptive Compression for On-Device Sparsely-Activated Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: The rise of the agentic web has been accompanied by growing demand for on-device Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that perform diverse cross-modal web tasks with enhanced privacy and reduced latency.
